伦敦，7月4日电。外交部次长R. A. 巴特勒先生昨日在下议院宣布，外交大臣哈利法克斯勋爵刚刚收到关于贝特伦·利里（Bertram Lillie）先生死亡一案的验尸程序报告；利里先生于4月24日在上海虹口的一起车祸中丧生。巴特勒称，在全面审议之前，他无法说明将采取何种适当行动。
他补充说，驻上海英国总领事已向日方同行递交照会，就导致这一悲剧的事件保留所有权利。
诺丁汉郡巴塞特劳选区的工党议员F. J. 贝伦杰先生询问，英国在此事中是否有任何金钱权益，以及是否可能以利里先生遗孀的名义提出某种损害赔偿要求。
巴特勒先生回答说，这是问题的一个重要方面，当然会被铭记在心。——路透社。

JUN 16 1939

Sergeant Wimsett Concludes
Lillie Inquest Evidence

Steering Wheel Grabbed by Japanese Sentry with
Both Hands ; Verdict to Be Given Today

WALKING with the aid of crutches following serious injuries sustained in an accident on Broadway near Minghong Road on April 24 when Mr. Bertram Lillie, principal of the Lester School and Henry Lester Institute, and a Japanese sailor sentry, were killed, Sergeant Ronald John Wimsett, of the Shanghai Municipal Police, yesterday gave his version of the accident before Mr. C. H. Haines, H. M. Coroner. His was the last testimony to be taken at the enquiry, which commenced on April 25, and a verdict will be delivered at 10 a.m. today. Substantiating the evidence of Mrs. Lillie, who was sitting beside Sergeant Wimsett in her husband's car when it was struck by a Japanese bus, he described the actions of the dead sentry in jumping on the running board and seizing the steering wheel with both hands.

Present at the enquiry were Mr. H. H. Thomas, Consul for Japanese Affairs, and Mr. R. F. C. Master, who represented the Henry Lester Trustees and Mrs. Lillie. First witness to give evidence was Sub-Inspector John James Gavan, who described the measurements from Broadway Bridge, west side, to the scene of the accident. The distance, he said, was 794 feet. The Japanese sentry's post was in the centre of the bridge.

Seated throughout his testimony, Sergeant Wimsett told the Coroner that on April 24 he was on duty at Garden Bridge. Between 8.30 and 8.40 p.m. he noticed a large dark saloon car crossing the bridge from north to south. Witness was standing on the footpath at the south end of the bridge and, as the car came opposite to him, it pulled over to where he was standing.

The occupants of the car—a foreign woman and man, whom he now knew as Mr. and Mrs. Lillie—alighted from the vehicle and Mrs. Lillie reported to him that just previously the car had been involved in an accident on the other side of the bridge. She stated that the car had collided with a barrier but did not know the exact locality. Both Mr. and Mrs. Lillie then went to the front of the car, where the former pointed out the damage which had been done to the vehicle.

Did Not Stop

Sergeant Wimsett continued that after Mr. Lillie had done this, he went on to say that, after colliding with the barrier, the car did not stop. Witness then suggested that they should return to the scene of the accident. "I had in my mind at the time," he said, "that someone might have been injured." It was his duty to go to the scene to get all information.

Both Mr. and Mrs. Lillie had agreed to do this with no show of reluctance and Mrs. Lillie and witness then entered the rear of the car with Mr. Lillie occupying the driver's seat. The car was turned around and it proceeded back over Garden Bridge from south to north along Seward Road. It had almost reached the intersection of Seward and Boone Roads when Mrs. Lillie told her husband that this was not the place.

Witness then suggested turning to the right which would bring them to the intersection of Boone Road and Broadway. Here Mrs. Lillie recognized Broadway Bridge and indicated that this was the place. They turned left and pulled up at a barrier almost on the crown of the bridge.

Very Agitated

Mrs. Lillie and he alighted and he walked towards a Japanese sentry on the south side of the bridge. "I pointed to the damage on the car and to the barrier," Sergeant Wimsett continued, "and the sentry looked to another sentry standing on the opposite side of the bridge This sentry came across and directed the car to be parked on Dixwell Road and this was done."

He added that the vehicle was parked facing Broadway and during the operation Mrs. Lillie exclaimed several times to the sentry "There are no lights on these barriers." He believed that the sentry did not understand what she was saying. "I looked at the barriers and I did not see any lights," he stated.

Mr. Lillie then alighted from the car and he appeared to be very agitated, Sergeant Wimsett continued. He appeared to be deeply concerned over the damage to his car, saying to the sentry "What are you going to do about the damage to my car?"

Broken English

Witness then went to a Japanese sentry and another Japanese sentry, in broken English and with a motion of his hand, indicated that he would telephone for, witness believed, an interpreter. Approaching Mr. Lillie witness informed him that they would have to wait until such time as an interpreter arrived. "Although Mr. Lillie appeared more normal at this time—he was not shouting but using a normal tone—he stated 'I'm not going to wait around here'," witness stated.

After being informed that if he did not wish to wait they had better go to Hongkew Police station, Mr. Lillie got back into the car and witness intimated to the Japanese that they were going to Hongkew Police station. The sentry then said something which he did not understand and made a motion with his hand. During all this Mrs. Lillie had already entered the car and had invited witness to get in also. He got in and sat beside her.

1939年6月16日

温姆塞特警士结束
利里案验尸证词

日本哨兵双手抓住方向盘；裁决将于今日宣布

莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特学院校长贝特伦·利里先生与一名日本水兵哨兵于4月24日在靠近明宏路（音译）的百老汇路发生事故身亡，上海公共租界警务处罗纳德·约翰·温姆塞特（Ronald John Wimsett）警士因在该事故中受重伤，昨日拄着拐杖出庭，向英王陛下验尸官C. H. 海恩斯先生陈述了他对事故经过的说法。他的证词是自4月25日开始调查以来最后采集的证言，裁决将于今日上午10时宣布。温姆塞特警士的证词证实了利里夫人的证据；事故发生时，利里夫人正坐在丈夫的车内，位于温姆塞特警士身旁，车辆被一辆日本巴士撞击。他描述了已故哨兵跳上脚踏板并用双手抓住方向盘的动作。

出席调查的还有日本事务领事H. H. 托马斯先生，以及代表亨利·莱斯特信托人和利里夫人的R. F. C. 马斯特先生。第一位作证的是副督察约翰·詹姆斯·加万（John James Gavan），他描述了从外白渡桥西侧到事故现场的距离。他说，这段距离为794英尺。日本哨兵的岗哨位于桥中央。

温姆塞特警士在整个作证过程中一直坐着，他告诉验尸官，4月24日他在外白渡桥执勤。晚上8点30分至8点40分之间，他注意到一辆大型深色轿车从北向南过桥。证人站在桥南端的人行道上，当车驶到他对面时，靠边停在他站立的位置。

车内乘客——一男一女两名外国人，他现在知道是利里夫妇——下车后，利里夫人向他报告说，刚才车子在桥的另一侧发生了事故。她声称车子撞上了障碍物，但不知道确切地点。随后利里夫妇走到车头，利里先生指出了车辆受损的情况。

未停车

温姆塞特警士继续说，利里先生这样做之后，接着说，撞上障碍物后，车子并没有停下。证人随后建议他们返回事故现场。“我当时心想，”他说，“可能有人受伤了。”他有责任去现场获取所有信息。

利里夫妇都同意这样做，没有丝毫犹豫，利里夫人和证人随后进入车后座，利里先生坐在驾驶座上。车子掉头，沿西华德路（Seward Road）由南向北再次驶过外白渡桥。当车子快要到达西华德路与布恩路（Boone Road）的交叉口时，利里夫人告诉丈夫这里不是那个地方。

证人随后建议向右转，这样他们就会到达布恩路与百老汇路的交叉口。在这里，利里夫人认出了外白渡桥，并指出就是这个地方。他们向左转，停在几乎位于桥顶的一个障碍物前。

非常激动

利里夫人和他下了车，他走向桥南侧的一名日本哨兵。“我指着车上的损坏处和障碍物，”温姆塞特警士继续说，“哨兵看向站在桥另一侧的另一名哨兵。这名哨兵走过来，指示将车停在狄思威路（Dixwell Road），于是照办了。”

他补充说，车辆停放时车头朝向百老汇路，在此期间，利里夫人多次对哨兵喊道：“这些障碍物上没有灯。”他认为哨兵听不懂她在说什么。“我看了那些障碍物，我没有看到任何灯光，”他陈述道。

利里先生随后下车，他显得非常激动，温姆塞特警士继续说。他似乎对车辆的损坏深感忧虑，对哨兵说：“你打算怎么处理我车的损坏问题？”

蹩脚的英语

证人随后走向一名日本哨兵，另一名日本哨兵用蹩脚的英语并配合手势表示，据证人相信，他将打电话叫一名翻译来。证人走近利里先生，告诉他他们必须等待翻译到来。“虽然利里先生此时显得比较正常——他没有大喊大叫，而是用正常的语调——但他说‘我不会在这里干等’，”证人陈述道。

在被告知如果不想等待，最好去虹口警察局后，利里先生回到车上，证人向日本人示意他们要去虹口警察局。哨兵随后说了一些他听不懂的话，并做了一个手势。在此期间，利里夫人已经上车，并邀请证人也上车。他上了车，坐在她旁边。

The Coroner--Was an interpreter
produced by the Japanese?
Sergeant Wimsett--I did not see
one but there may have been one. I
saw no civilian there at all.
Mr. Lillie, he stated, drove the car
towards the crown of the bridge very
slowly and witness opened the door
so that he could speak to the Japan-
ese sentry on the crown of the bridge.
When they arrived there he indicated
that they were going to Hongkew
Police station and he pointed in that
direction.
At this time the car was going down
the incline at a faster speed and he
closed the door. The two Japanese
sentries then jumped on the running
board near the driver's door, one on
the left side and one on the right side.
"The sentry on the right side of
the car grabbed hold of the steering
wheel with both hands," Sergeant
Wimsett continued, "and at the same
time I saw the sentry on the left
bend his body through the window
and reach towards the driving wheel.
Mr. Lillie then took his left arm off
the wheel and warded off the Japan-
ese sentry's reach. This sentry then
took up the position he was in be-
fore--an upright position on the run-
ning board.
Zig-Zagging
Mr. Lillie by this time had put the
car in second gear and the vehicle
was travelling in a zig-zag fashion
down Broadway, going from one side
of the road to the other. The sentry
on the right was pulling the wheel,
first to the left and then to the right,
and Mr. Lillie was working against
him. Mrs. Lillie and myself shouted
'Stop'. "Sergeant Wimsett went on,'
but Mr. Lillie did not reply. We had
almost reached the intersection of
Tsingpoo Road and at that time the
front left wheel and the rear left
wheel mounted the left footpath.
"The car then swung back on to
the roadway and the sudden jolting
threw me forward. I struck my nose
on the back of the seat where Mr.
Lillie was sitting and I don't remem-
ber what happened until I awoke and
found myself in hospital." In answer
to Mr. Haines, he stated that that car
at the time would be travelling at
about 15 m.p.h., the road being "al-
most quite dry."
He did not see Mr. Lillie make any
attempt to stop the car although he
imagined there was plenty of opport-
unity for him to have done so. He
could have put his foot on the brake.
witness added. Mr. Lillie, he said,
was absolutely sober at the time and
he was not in an angry mood.
In adjourning the enquiry until
today Mr. Haines stated "I have taken
all the evidence we have been able
to obtain in this enquiry and I do not
propose to give my decision today.
I will give this tomorrow before pro-
ceeding with the other (R. M. Tinkler)
inquest."

验尸官——日本人派出翻译了吗？
温姆塞特警士——我没看见，但可能有。我根本没看到那里有平民。
他说，利里先生非常缓慢地将车开向桥顶，证人打开车门，以便能与桥顶的日本哨兵说话。当他们到达那里时，他示意他们要去虹口警察局，并指向那个方向。
此时车子正以更快的速度下坡，他关上了车门。两名日本哨兵随后跳上靠近驾驶座车门的脚踏板，一人在左侧，一人在右侧。
“右侧的哨兵用双手抓住了方向盘，”温姆塞特警士继续说，“同时我看到左侧的哨兵弯下身子穿过车窗，伸手去抓方向盘。利里先生随后将左臂从方向盘上移开，挡开了日本哨兵的抓取。这名哨兵随即恢复了他之前的姿势——直立在脚踏板上。”
曲折行驶
此时利里先生已将车挂入二档，车辆在百老汇路上呈曲折状行驶，从道路的一侧摆到另一侧。右侧的哨兵先是向左拉方向盘，然后又向右拉，利里先生则与他对抗。利里夫人和我大喊“停车”。温姆塞特警士接着说，“但利里先生没有回应。我们几乎到达了青岛路（Tsingpoo Road）的交叉口，当时左前轮和左后轮冲上了左侧人行道。”
“车子随后甩回路面，剧烈的颠簸将我向前抛去。我的鼻子撞在了利里先生坐的座椅靠背上，直到我在医院醒来，我才记起之后发生了什么。”在回答海恩斯先生的提问时，他表示当时车速约为每小时15英里，路面“几乎完全干燥”。
他没有看到利里先生试图停车，尽管他想象有利里先生停车的充分机会。证人补充说，他本可以踩刹车。他说，利里先生当时绝对清醒，并没有处于愤怒状态。
海恩斯先生在宣布将调查延期至今日时表示：“我已经听取了我们在本次调查中所能获得的所有证据，我不打算今天作出裁决。我将在明天继续进行另一起（R. M. Tinkler）案件的验尸之前作出裁决。”

“Lillie Should
Have Stopped
Car” – Coroner
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
Death Of Briton Aided
By Own Rash
Actions
JUN 16 1939
JAPANESEN SEN'RY
ACT CONTRIBUTED
Verdict In HBM Court
Inquest Rendered
By C. H. Haines

Mr. Bertram Lillie contributed
to his death by his rash act, and
should have stopped the car when
the Japanese sentry struggled
with the steering wheel, while
the sentry also contributed to Mr.
Lillie's death by his rash act in
pulling at the wheel. So stated
Mr. C. H. Haines, Registrar of
HBM Court, in giving his verdict
this morning at the inquest on
Mr. Lillie, principal of the Lester
Technical Institute.

Mr. Haines, reviewed the
evidence before giving his verdict
this morning. He pointed out
that both Mrs. Lillie and Police
Sergeant R. J. Wimsett had asked
Lillie to halt the car. He also
told the court that he had asked
the Japanese Consulate-General
for one of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party to give evidence
but that unfortunately he did not
appear.

Bus Driver Exonerated
The Coroner exonerated the bus
driver, in his finding that Mr.
Bertram Lillie died as a result of
injuries received between his
motor car and a bus on Broad-
way near Minghong Road at 9
p.m. on April 24.

Sergeant Ronald J. Wimsett of
the SMP, who was injured dur-
ing the crash, and who has been
in the hospital since the night of
the tragedy, testified that a
Japanese sentry was pulling at
the steering wheel of the Lillie
car just before it crashed into the
omnibus.

Report Made
The police officer said that he
had been on duty on the Garden
Bridge on the night of the ac-
cident, between 8.30 and 8.40 p.m.
when the Lillie car drove up. Mr.
and Mrs. Lillie alighted and said
that their car had ran into a
barrier but that they did not
know the exact location.

Sergeant Wimsett got into the
car with the Lillies and went
down Broadway until they reach-
ed the barrier. There were no
lights on the barrier. Mr. Lillie
appeared to be greatly concerned
over the damage done to his car
and asked the Japanese sentry
at the barrier what he was going
to do about it.

Sentries Pull Wheel
The party then got back in the
car to proceed to Hongkew police
station to wait for a Japanese
interpreter. At the same time
two Japanese sentries jumped on
the running board of the car, just
as it got underway. One of the
sentries kept pushing and pulling
at the steering wheel.

Mrs. Lillie and the police officer
shouted at Mr. Lillie to stop the
car, but he paid no attention,
keeping his mind on his driving
and trying to ward off the Japan-
ese sentry, said Sergeant Wimsett.
Then the crash came and Wim-
sett was knocked unconscious.

“利里本应
停车”——验尸官
《上海晚邮报及信使报》。
英国人之死部分归因于
其自身的鲁莽
行为
1939年6月16日
日本哨兵
的行为亦有责任
英王陛下法院
验尸裁决由
C. H. 海恩斯作出

莱斯特技术学院校长利里先生因其鲁莽行为促成了自己的死亡，当日本哨兵争夺方向盘时，他本应停车；而哨兵因拉扯方向盘的鲁莽行为，也促成了利里先生的死亡。英王陛下法院书记官C. H. 海恩斯先生在今日上午对利里先生的验尸调查中作出上述裁决。

海恩斯先生在上午作出裁决前回顾了证据。他指出，利里夫人和警务处R. J. 温姆塞特警士都曾要求利里停车。他还告诉法庭，他曾要求日本总领事馆派出一名日本海军陆战队队员作证，但不幸的是该人未出庭。

巴士司机被免除责任

验尸官在其裁定中指出，贝特伦·利里先生死于4月24日晚9时在靠近明宏路（音译）的百老汇路上，其汽车与一辆巴士之间碰撞所造成的伤害，并免除了巴士司机的责任。

上海公共租界警务处的罗纳德·J. 温姆塞特警士在车祸中受伤，自悲剧发生当晚起一直住院，他作证说，在利里的汽车撞上公共汽车之前，一名日本哨兵正在拉扯利里汽车的方向盘。

已作报告

这位警官说，事故发生当晚8点30分至8点40分之间，他正在外白渡桥执勤，当时利里的车开了过来。利里夫妇下车后说，他们的车撞上了障碍物，但他们不知道确切位置。

温姆塞特警士与利里夫妇一同上车，沿百老汇路下行，直到他们到达障碍物处。障碍物上没有灯光。利里先生似乎对车辆受到的损坏非常关切，并询问障碍物处的日本哨兵打算如何处理。

哨兵拉扯方向盘

随后众人回到车上，准备前往虹口警察局等待日本翻译。与此同时，就在车子启动时，两名日本哨兵跳上了车的脚踏板。其中一名哨兵不停地推拉拉扯方向盘。

温姆塞特警士说，利里夫人和这位警官曾大声呼喊利里先生停车，但他不予理会，一心驾驶，并试图挡开日本哨兵。随后发生了碰撞，温姆塞特被撞昏过去。

JUN 7 1930
LILLIE INQUEST IS ADJOURNED
Sergt. Wimsett's Evidence
Needed Before The
Decision
The inquest on the death of Mr.
Bertram Lillie, late principal of the
Henry Lester Institute who was
killed in a motor accident on
Broadway, on the night of April
24, was continued in the British
Police Court yesterday afternoon.
However, no evidence was given,
and the case was adjourned until
Thursday June 15, when Sergeant
Wimsett, who was in the car in-
volved in the collision, will be out
of hospital.
His evidence is very important
to the coroner, for he is one of the
two witnesses who can tell the
court what happened before the
accident. The only other person
who was in the accident and can
tell of the events leading up to it,
is Mrs. Lillie, who gave evidence
last week. It will be remembered
that she told H. M. Coroner C. H.
Haines about the Japanese sentry
jumping on the running board of
Mr. Lillie's car and pulling the
steering wheel just before the
crash.
In the collision with the Japan-
ese motor bus, Mr. Lillie and the
Japanese sentry were killed, and
Mrs. Lillie and Sergt. Wimsett were
injured. Mrs. Lillie left hospital
last week, shortly before she ap-
peared in court, but Sergt. Wimsett
will have to remain in hospital for
another fortnight. Besides Sergt.
Wimsett, the Police officer, who
measured the distance between
Broadway bridge and the scene of
the accident, will appear in court
on June 15.

利里死因研讯延期
在作出裁决前需听取温塞特警士的证词
关于亨利·雷士德工学院前院长伯特伦·利里（Bertram Lillie）先生于4月24日晚在百老汇路车祸中丧生一案的死因研讯，昨日下午在英国警察法庭继续进行。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
MAY 26 1939

Mrs. Lillie Relates Story of
Fatal Crash on Broadway

Japanese Sentry Said to Have Jumped on Car and
Pulled Steering Wheel in Path of Bus

GIVING her account of the accident which caused the death of
her husband, Mr. Bertram Lillie, Principal of the Lester
School and Henry Lester Technical Institute, on Broadway near
Minghong Road on the night of April 24, Mrs. Marjorie Lillie
yesterday told Mr. C. H. Haines, H. M. Coroner, that the fatal
collision between Mr. Lillie's car and a Japanese-owned bus was
caused by the action of a Japanese sentry, who jumped on the
running board of the car and pulled the steering wheel so that
the vehicle shot across the road in the path of the oncoming
bus. It will be recalled that the sentry was killed in the colli-
sion while Sergeant R. J. Wimsett of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, who was a passenger in the car, was seriously injured.

Mrs. Lillie, who was allowed to
sit down while giving her evidence,
stated that at about 6.30 or 6.45 p.m.
on April 24 Mr. H. F. Prytherch (his
evidence was taken at a former sit-
ting) called at her husband's home
at 401 Great Western Road and
offered to give them a lift in his
car to East Seward Road as they had
been unable to get a taxi. After
driving there without any incident
Mr. Lillie found his car awaiting him
and he drove it to the Shanghai and
Hongkew Wharf with witness sitting
in Mr. Prytherch's car, which was
following.

At the wharf all three went on
board the ss. Gneisenau to look for
two pipes which, her husband stated,
he had left on the ship. They were
unable to find the pipes and they
stayed on the ship for 15 or 20
minutes, during which time they had
two cocktails each. When they left
the boat it would be getting on for
eight o'clock, Mrs. Lillie added.

Mr. Prytherch drove away first in
his car but witness and her husband
did not follow as their car had to
be turned around before it was able
to leave the wharf. With her hus-
band driving, the car then came out
of the wharf and turned left up
Broadway.

"When we got to Broadway
Bridge," Mrs. Lillie continued, "we
did not see anything until we heard
a crash. Evidently there were two
barriers across the road and we hit
one of these which was jutting out
more than the other." She added
that the barriers were not of the
barbed wire type but consisted of
wire mesh on a frame. The glass in
the right headlamp was broken as
a result of the accident.

Barrier Knocked Down

"No-one attempted to stop us, so
we went a little slower and drove
on," she added, "and I looked back
and saw two men picking the barrier
up. They were dressed in dark
uniforms and I thought they were
Japanese." After driving down Broad-
way and over Garden Bridge her
husband turned around at the traffic
lights near the British Consulate and
reported the accident to a policeman
whom she knew now to have been
Sergeant Wimsett.

After informing the policeman of
the accident and showing him the
broken lamp, he informed witness
and her husband that it would be
better to go to the scene of the ac-
cident and then to Hongkew Police

Station. Asked if he was coming
with them he said that he would and
witness got into the back seat with
him, a thing she had never done
before.

On arrival at the bridge the Japan-
ese sentries made them cross over
the bridge and park the car alongside
the creek with the bonnet facing the
Whangpoo River, Mrs. Lillie stated.
After taking out a notebook a sentry
took the number of the car and
Sergeant Wimsett tried to talk to
them but they did not understand.
Witness heard the word "interpreter"
and a Japanese in civilian clothes
came on the scene very quickly. As
this man did not seem to understand,
Sergeant Wimsett stated that they
would go to Hongkew Police Station
and pointed in that direction.

Jumped on Car

"As soon as Hongkew Police Station
was mentioned," she said, "one of
them tried to take the ignition key
out of the car but he could not reach
it and so he did not bother any
more." Sergeant Wimsett then stat-
ed that he would take the interpreter
to Hongkew Police Station but the
interpreter did not get into the car
although they left the door open.

"As soon as Sergeant Wimsett
shut the door Mr. Lillie started to
drive off. We had to drive out of
the creek and turn right the barrier
to come into Broadway again," she
continued. "When we were going
down the incline the sentry jumped
on the right hand side of the car.
Without a word of warning he
caught hold of the steering wheel
and the car shot right across the
road to the right hand side. Mr.
Lillie tried to get the car back on
the left hand side but the wheel was
pulled again and the car again went
to the right hand side of the road."

Continuing Mrs. Lillie stated "It
was then that the sentry shouted
'Stop' in English but no sooner had
he spoken than he pulled the wheel
again and Mr. Lillie could not control
the car. When the Japanese sentry
shouted 'Stop' I turned round and
told him to stop but he did not. If
he had done so Mr. Lillie would have
been able to right the car. It was
while he was pulling the wheel and
we had shot across the road that a
bus appeared. Mr. Lillie must have
seen the bus coming because he
quickly pulled the car round so that
it could not hit my side and it hit
his side. We did not see it until
it was right on top of us."

《字林西报》，
1939年5月26日

利里夫人讲述百老汇路致命车祸经过

据称日本哨兵跳上汽车并拉扯方向盘，致使车辆驶入公共汽车路径

马乔里·利里（Marjorie Lillie）夫人昨日向英王陛下验尸官 C. H. 海恩斯先生陈述了其丈夫——雷士德学校及亨利·雷士德技术学院院长伯特伦·利里先生——于4月24日晚在靠近明宏路（Minghong Road）的百老汇路遭遇车祸身亡的事故经过。她表示，利里先生的汽车与一辆日资公共汽车之间的致命碰撞，是由一名日本哨兵的行为造成的，该哨兵跳上汽车脚踏板并拉扯方向盘，导致车辆横穿马路，驶入迎面驶来的公共汽车路径。据悉，该哨兵在碰撞中身亡，而当时作为车内乘客的上海公共租界工部局警务处 R. J. 温塞特（R. J. Wimsett）警士则受重伤。

利里夫人在作证时被允许坐着，她陈述道，4月24日下午约6点30分或6点45分，H. F. 普里瑟奇（H. F. Prytherch）先生（其证词已在之前的庭审中采集）来到她位于大西路401号的家中，提出用他的车送他们去东熙华德路，因为他们未能叫到出租车。在毫无事故地驾车到达那里后，利里先生发现他的车在等他，于是他驾驶自己的车前往上海与虹口码头，证人则坐在随后跟随的普里瑟奇先生的车里。

在码头，三人均登上“格奈森瑙”号（ss. Gneisenau）轮船，寻找她丈夫声称留在船上的两根管子。他们未能找到管子，在船上停留了15或20分钟，期间每人喝了两杯鸡尾酒。利里夫人补充说，当他们离开船时，时间已接近八点。

普里瑟奇先生先驾车离开，但证人和其丈夫并未跟随，因为他们的车在离开码头前需要掉头。随后，由她丈夫驾驶，车辆驶出码头并向左转上百老汇路。

“当我们到达百老汇桥时，”利里夫人继续说道，“直到听到撞击声我们才看到任何东西。显然路上有两道路障，我们撞上了其中突出较多的一道。”她补充说，这些路障并非铁丝网类型，而是由框架上的金属网构成。事故导致右侧前大灯的玻璃破碎。

路障被撞倒

“没有人试图拦停我们，所以我们稍微放慢速度继续行驶，”她补充道，“我回头看到两名男子正在扶起路障。他们身穿深色制服，我以为他们是日本人。”在沿百老汇路行驶并经过外白渡桥后，她丈夫在英国领事馆附近的交通信号灯处掉头，并向一名警察报告了事故，她现在知道那名警察是温塞特警士。

在向警察告知事故并展示破损的车灯后，他告诉证人和其丈夫，最好先返回事故现场，然后再去虹口捕房。当被问及他是否同行时，他说他会去，证人便与他一起坐进后座，这是她以前从未做过的事。

利里夫人陈述道，到达桥头时，日本哨兵让他们过桥，并将车停在河边，车头朝向黄浦江。一名哨兵拿出笔记本记下汽车号码，温塞特警士试图与他们交谈，但他们听不懂。证人听到“翻译”一词，一名身穿便服的日本人很快来到现场。由于此人似乎也不明白，温塞特警士表示他们将前往虹口捕房，并指向那个方向。

跳上汽车

“只要一提到虹口捕房，”她说，“其中一人就试图从车上拔出点火钥匙，但他够不着，所以就不再纠缠。”温塞特警士随后表示他将带翻译去虹口捕房，但尽管车门开着，翻译并未上车。

“温塞特警士一关上车门，利里先生就开始驾车离开。我们必须驶离河边，向右绕过路障，重新进入百老汇路，”她继续说道。“当我们下坡时，那名哨兵跳上汽车右侧。他毫无预警地抓住方向盘，汽车猛地横穿马路冲向右侧。利里先生试图将车开回左侧，但方向盘再次被拉扯，汽车又冲向了马路右侧。”

利里夫人继续陈述：“就在那时，哨兵用英语大喊‘停下’，但他话音未落又拉扯方向盘，利里先生无法控制汽车。当日本哨兵大喊‘停下’时，我转过身让他停下，但他没有。如果他停下了，利里先生本能够纠正车辆方向。正当他拉扯方向盘、我们横穿马路时，一辆公共汽车出现了。利里先生一定看到了公共汽车驶来，因为他迅速转动汽车，使其不会撞到我这一侧，而是撞到了他那一侧。直到公共汽车几乎压在我们身上时，我们才看到它。”

pages.en:
Bad Lighting

Witness stated that the bus had
blue discs on the headlights which
were not bright. The street lighting
in the vicinity was very bad. The
bus, she added, hit them with a
terrible crash and she was injured
on the head. Their car at the time
of the impact had been almost at a
standstill on the wrong side of the
road. When the sentry jumped on to
their car they were not travelling at
a fast speed nor did she tell her hus-
band to stop as he was concentrating
on driving.
The first witness to be called at
yesterday's sitting, Jacob J. Pavloff,
stated that he was a watchman
employed by the Asia Realty Co. at
Lane 179 Broadway. Just after 9
p.m. on April 24 he was on duty at
his post inside the alley when he
saw a car passing at about 25 to 30
m.p.h. As soon as it had passed he
heard a crash and he saw that the
vehicle had collided with a bus, the
number of which was A14.
Witness then heard a woman crying
in the car and with the help of two
Italian marines they placed her on
the pavement. Also inside the car,
sitting next to the lady, was a for-
eigner in dark clothes, while in the
front, lying on the seat, was another
foreigner who appeared to be dead.
After going to call an ambulance
witness returned to the scene about
five or six minutes afterwards and
he saw the foreign lady on the
pavement with a police sergeant and
a civilian.

Doctor's Evidence

In order to remove a man who
had been squeezed between the car
and the bus and who was found to
be a Japanese marine, the car had
to be moved. This man was placed
on the pavement and then taken
away.
Foreign Sergeant R. J. N. MacKay
of the Vehicle Inspection Office,
Shanghai Municipal Police gave evid-
ence of examining Mr. Lillie's car.
The steering wheel, he stated, was
twisted and cracked while the steer-
ing column was bent just above the
steering box. There was nothing to
show that there had been any defect
in the steering mechanism. All the
brakes were intact except the left
rear brake. This was disconnected,
the rod being badly bent but the
connection joint was not damaged. He
had come to the conclusion that it
had been disconnected after the ac-
cident to release the brakes, which
were in working order.
Dr. I. G. Anderson, who conducted
a post mortem examination on the
body of Mr. Lillie, stated that death
had been caused by a rupture of
the aorta, which had been penetrated
by a broken rib. All the fixed ribs
on the right side of the body had been
broken and death was instantaneous.
The enquiry was then adjourned
until Wednesday at 2.15 p.m.
pages.zh:
照明不良

证人陈述，公共汽车的前大灯上有蓝色圆盘，光线不亮。附近的街道照明非常糟糕。她补充说，公共汽车以可怕的撞击力撞上他们，她的头部受伤。在撞击发生时，他们的汽车几乎静止在马路的错误一侧。当哨兵跳上他们的车时，车速并不快，她也没有让丈夫停车，因为他正专注于驾驶。
昨日庭审传唤的第一位证人雅各布·J·帕夫洛夫（Jacob J. Pavloff）陈述，他是受雇于亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Co.）的看守，工作地点在百老汇路179弄。4月24日晚9点刚过，他在巷内的岗位上执勤时，看到一辆汽车以约25至30英里的时速驶过。车刚一驶过，他就听到一声撞击声，并看到该车辆与一辆公共汽车相撞，车牌号为A14。
证人随后听到车内有一名妇女在哭泣，在两名意大利海军陆战队员的帮助下，他们将她安置在人行道上。车内还有一名身穿深色衣服的外国人坐在女士旁边，而前排座位上躺着另一名外国人，看似已死亡。
证人前去呼叫救护车后，约五六分钟后返回现场，他看到那名外国女士在人行道上，旁边有一名警士和一名平民。

医生证词

为了移出一名被挤在汽车和公共汽车之间的人（经查为一名日本海军陆战队员），必须移动汽车。此人被放置在人行道上，随后被带走。
上海公共租界工部局警务处车辆检验所的外籍警士 R. J. N. 麦凯（R. J. N. MacKay）就检查利里先生汽车一事作证。他陈述，方向盘扭曲且破裂，转向柱在转向器上方弯曲。没有任何迹象表明转向机构存在缺陷。所有刹车均完好无损，除了左后刹车。该刹车已断开，连杆严重弯曲，但连接接头未受损。他得出的结论是，这是在事故后为释放处于工作状态的刹车而断开的。
对利里先生尸体进行尸检的 I. G. 安德森（I. G. Anderson）医生陈述，死因是主动脉破裂，主动脉被一根断裂的肋骨刺穿。身体右侧的所有固定肋骨均断裂，死亡是瞬间发生的。
随后，调查休庭至星期三下午2点15分。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

MAY 25 1939

Lillie Auto Stated
In Good Condition
Prior To Accident

Little was revealed at the re-
sumption of the inquest into the
death of Mr. Bertram Lillie,
Lester Institute head who met his
death when a Japanese bus col-
lided with the car he was driving
on Broadway on April 24, by the
two witnesses who testified before
the Coroner, Mr. C. H. Haines, in
HBM court this morning.
First to rush to the scene of
the wreck, Jacob Pavloff, Russian
watchman, heard the crash from
his post at Lane 179, Broadway.
He did not see the accident, how-
ever, as it occurred around the
corner and out of his vision. With
the aid of two Italian marines who
arrived on the scene, Mr. Pavloff
removed Mrs. Lillie from the rear
of the car and extricated the
Japanese marine from between the
bus and the motor car, where he
had been pinned.
Sergant Roderick McKay of the
Vehicle Inspection Office of the
SMP testified that he had ex-
amined the Lillie car on May 2,
about eight days after the wreck,
and that in his opinion there had
been nothing wrong with either the
steering gear of the brakes prior
to the accident.
The inquest was adjourned until
2.15 this afternoon, when evidence
was to be given by Dr. Anderson
and Mrs. Lillie.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。

1939年5月26日

据称利里汽车在
事故前状况良好

今天上午，在英王陛下法庭，就4月24日利里先生在百老汇路驾驶的汽车与一辆日本公共汽车相撞致死一案的死因研讯恢复审理，两名证人在验尸官 C. H. 海恩斯先生面前作证，但披露的信息甚少。
最先赶到事故现场的俄罗斯看守雅各布·帕夫洛夫（Jacob Pavloff）在百老汇路179弄的岗位上听到了撞击声。然而，他并未看到事故，因为事故发生在拐角处，不在他的视线范围内。在抵达现场的两名意大利海军陆战队员的协助下，帕夫洛夫先生将利里夫人从车后部救出，并将被卡在公共汽车和汽车之间的日本海军陆战队员解救出来。
上海公共租界工部局警务处车辆检验所的罗德里克·麦凯（Roderick McKay）警士作证称，他于5月2日，即事故后约八天，检查了利里汽车，他认为在事故前，转向装置或刹车均无任何问题。
死因研讯休庭至今日下午2点15分，届时将由安德森医生和利里夫人提供证词。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

MAY 23 1939

Inquest on Mr. Bertram Lillie
Continues in H.M. Court

Witness States Speed of Japanese Bus Excessive;
Japanese Sentry Holding Steering Wheel

TESTIFYING at the resumed inquest held on the late Mr. Bertram
Lillie, Principal of the Lester School and Henry Lester
Institute, before Mr. C. H. Haines, H. M. Coroner, yesterday, an
Iranian passenger in the Japanese-owned bus which collided with
Mr. Lillie's car on April 24 on Broadway, near Minghong Road,
stated that this vehicle was travelling at an excessive speed which
he estimated to be between 45 and 50 miles an hour. After con-
cluding his evidence, he added that the Japanese marine, who had
been crushed between the bus and Mr. Lillie's car and had been
killed by the impact, was seen by him to be gripping the steering
wheel of the car with his left hand.

Mrs. Lillie, who was injured during
the collision, did not appear in court
and at the conclusion of the evidence
it was pointed out that Sergeant
R. J. Winsett of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police, also a passenger in the
car, would not be able to leave hos-
pital for three weeks. Mr. H. H.
Thomas, H. M. Consul for Japanese
Affairs, attended the enquiry, while
Mr. R. F. C. Master appeared on
behalf of the Henry Lester Trustees
and Mrs. Lillie. Also present were
several Japanese, two of whom took
notes of the evidence.

The first witness, Mr. Henry Frede-
rick Prytherch, of the Shanghai
Waterworks Co., 484 Kiangse Road,
told the Coroner that at 6.45 p.m.
on April 24 he went to Mr. Lillie's
home on Great Western Road to greet
him, after his return from England.
During a conversation Mr. Lillie told
witness that he would have to return
to the ss. Gneisenau (the ship which
had brought him to Shanghai on the
same day) to find two pipes which
he had left on the vessel.

After failing to get a taxi witness
drove Mr. and Mrs. Lillie across the
Soochow Creek in his own car to the
Lester School in Seward Road, where
Mr. Lillie obtained his own car. With
Mrs. Lillie remaining in his car wit-
ness then drove after Mr. Lillie to
the Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf
where they went on board the
Gneisenau.

Barrier Not Lighted

After trying to open a cabin door,
witness continued, Mr. Lillie told a
passing steward that he had left two
pipes in the cabin and asked the man
to recover them. All three then went
to the smoke room where Mr. Lillie
ordered cocktails before they sat
down. After the steward had report-
ed that he could not find the pipes
they stayed for about 15 to 20 minutes,
during which time Mr. Lillie had two
cocktails.

After leaving the ship witness
drove away first in his own car but
did not see Mr. Lillie follow him.
Approaching Broadway Bridge wit-
ness pulled up his car as he knew
that there had been a barrier there
for some time. This, he noticed, had
been pulled into the left of the road
and there did not seem to be much
room to pass. After the sentry had
nodded him on he passed.

At this point Mr. Prytherch said
he was struck by the fact that the
barrier was not lighted and the only
notification of its presence was a
small notice board with Japanese or
Chinese characters written on it.
Questioned about the street lighting
Mr. Prytherch stated that it was
rather dark and that there was no
light shining on the barrier.

Witness, after driving over Garden
Bridge, parked his car outside the
Cathay Hotel. As he crossed the road
a car passed him and, thinking that
it was Mr. Lillie's car, he waved.
Answering the Coroner he stated that
Mr. Lillie had not had too much alco-
hol and he was in a normal state. He
added that Mr. Lillie was always
bright and cheerful and during the
eighteen months that he had known
him he had never known him to be
hasty. Questioned by Mr. Master,
witness stated that if Mr. Lillie had
not known that there was a barrier
on Broadway Bridge he would have
had great difficulty in avoiding it.

Mikhail J. Oghol, an Iranian sub-
ject, whose evidence was given in
Russian, stated that he was a merch-
ant living at 220 Kungping Road. At
about 9.15 p.m. he boarded a Japanese
bus near Broadway Mansions to pro-
ceed to his home. There were about
seven or eight passengers in the bus
and shortly after leaving Broadway
Mansions there was a collision be-
tween the bus and a car, which later
he discovered was owned by Mr.
Lillie.

"I did not see the actual accident
but I saw something dark in front
of the bus," he continued. "I was
sitting in the rear and I was thrown
forward to the driver's seat in front,
the driver already being on the floor.
I noticed a strong smell of petrol and
my first thought was to get off the
bus in case it caught fire. After try-
ing to get through the door I saw a
Chinese jump out of the window and
I followed." The Chinese conductress,
he said, was standing by the driver.

After leaving the bus witness added
that he did not pay any attention to
the damaged vehicles as both the car
and the bus were together and it was
impossible to see the damage owing
to the darkness. Shown a photograph
of the car and the bus, witness stated
that they were not in that position
at the time of the collision as the two
vehicles were moved later to extricate
the Japanese marine who was caught
between them.

On the footpath on the left side of
the road, he added, there were three
persons, two of whom—a police officer
and Mr. Lillie—were lying down
while a third person, Mrs. Lillie, was
sitting on the edge of the pavement
and crying "My handbag. My hand-
bag." Witness went to the car to
search for the handbag and after
noticing it in the vehicle saw that
someone was squeezed between the
car and the bus. After the man had
been released he noticed that he was
a Japanese marine.

《字林西报》，

1939年5月23日

伯特伦·利利先生死因研讯
在英国法庭继续进行

证人称日本公共汽车车速过快；
日本哨兵手握方向盘

昨日，在皇家验尸官 C. H. Haines 先生主持下，就莱斯特学校（Lester School）及亨利·莱斯特学院（Henry Lester Institute）校长、已故伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie）先生的死因研讯复庭。一名伊朗籍乘客作证称，4月24日，在靠近明宏路（Minghong Road）的百老汇路（Broadway）上，这辆属于日方的公共汽车与利利先生的汽车相撞。该证人表示，该车行驶速度过快，他估计时速在45至50英里之间。在完成证词后，他补充说，他看到那名被挤在公共汽车和利利先生汽车之间、因撞击而身亡的日本海军陆战队员，正用左手紧握着汽车的驾驶盘。

利利夫人在碰撞中受伤，未出庭。在举证结束时，有人指出，上海公共租界工部局警务处的 R. J. Winsett 巡长也是车内乘客，但他需三周后才能出院。负责日本事务的英国领事 H. H. Thomas 先生出席了研讯，R. F. C. Master 先生代表亨利·莱斯特信托基金（Henry Lester Trustees）及利利夫人出庭。现场还有数名日本人出席，其中两人对证词做了记录。

第一位证人，江西路484号上海自来水公司（Shanghai Waterworks Co.）的 Henry Frederick Prytherch 先生告诉验尸官，4月24日下午6时45分，他去大西路（Great Western Road）利利先生家中迎接其从英国归来。交谈中，利利先生告诉证人，他必须返回“格奈森瑙”号轮船（ss. Gneisenau，即当天载他抵达上海的船只），去取留在船上的两支烟斗。

由于未能叫到出租车，证人用自己的车送利利夫妇穿过苏州河，前往西华德路（Seward Road）的莱斯特学校，利利先生在那里取了自己的车。利利夫人留在证人的车里，证人随后驾车跟随利利先生前往上海虹口码头（Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf），他们登上了“格奈森瑙”号。

路障未设灯光

证人继续说道，利利先生试图打开一间客舱的门未果后，告诉一名路过的侍者，他把两支烟斗忘在客舱里了，请侍者去取回。三人随后去了吸烟室，利利先生在坐下前点了鸡尾酒。侍者回报说找不到烟斗后，他们停留了约15至20分钟，期间利利先生喝了两杯鸡尾酒。

离开轮船后，证人先驾自己的车离去，但未看到利利先生跟随。接近百老汇路桥时，证人停下车，因为他知道那里设置路障已有一段时间。他注意到路障已被拉至道路左侧，似乎没有太多空间通过。在哨兵点头示意后，他通过了路障。

Prytherch 先生在此时表示，令他印象深刻的是路障没有灯光照明，唯一提示其存在的标志是一块写有日文或中文的小告示牌。在被问及街道照明情况时，Prytherch 先生表示当时相当昏暗，路障上没有光线照射。

证人驾车经过外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）后，将车停在华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel）外。当他过马路时，一辆车从他身边驶过，他以为那是利利先生的车，便挥手致意。回答验尸官提问时，他表示利利先生饮酒不多，状态正常。他补充说，利利先生总是精神饱满、心情愉快，在他认识利利先生的十八个月里，从未见他行事鲁莽。经 Master 先生询问，证人表示，如果利利先生不知道百老汇路桥上有路障，他将很难避开它。

Mikhail J. Oghol，一名伊朗籍人士，其证词以俄语陈述，称他是居住在公平路（Kungping Road）220号的商人。晚上9点15分左右，他在百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions）附近登上一辆日本公共汽车回家。车上约有七八名乘客，离开百老汇大厦不久，公共汽车与一辆汽车发生碰撞，他后来得知该车为利利先生所有。

“我没有看到事故发生的瞬间，但我看到公共汽车前方有一个黑乎乎的东西，”他继续说道。“我坐在后排，被甩到了前面的驾驶座位置，司机已经倒在地板上。我闻到一股强烈的汽油味，我的第一反应是下车，以防车辆起火。在试图从车门出去时，我看到一名中国人从窗户跳了出去，我也跟着跳了下去。”他说，那名中国女售票员站在司机旁边。

证人补充说，离开公共汽车后，他没有注意受损的车辆，因为汽车和公共汽车撞在一起，且由于天色黑暗，无法看清损坏情况。在出示汽车和公共汽车的照片后，证人表示，碰撞发生时两车并非处于照片中的位置，因为后来为了救出被夹在中间的那名日本海军陆战队员，两辆车被移动过。

他补充说，在道路左侧的人行道上有三个人，其中两人——一名警官和利利先生——躺在地上，第三人利利夫人则坐在人行道边缘，哭喊着“我的手袋。我的手袋。”证人走向汽车寻找手袋，在车内看到手袋后，发现有人被挤在汽车和公共汽车之间。在那人获救后，他注意到那是一名日本海军陆战队员。

the handbag in the car he did not

手握方向盘

证人补充说，当他在车里看到手袋时，他没有触碰，决定等待警察到来。然而，一名意大利海军陆战队员捡起了手袋，并将其交给利利夫人。证人称，在那名日本海军陆战队员获救后，他倒在地上，随后被一群中国人抬走。

回答验尸官提问时，他表示，当他登上公共汽车时，天开始下雨，路面湿滑。公共汽车行驶速度非常快，左右摇晃。他估计时速

在45至50英里之间，最低为45英里。他表示，这是一个异常的速度，比这些公共汽车的通常速度快得多。他随后补充说，当他看到那名日本海军陆战队员位于汽车和公共汽车之间时，他的左手正握着汽车的驾驶盘。

Leopold Priefer，霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）1006号的一家餐馆老板，表示4月24日他乘坐一辆开往外白渡桥方向的公共汽车，途中车辆停下。他向外看，看到路上有两名男子和一名女士，并看到那位女士站起来，面部流血。汽车和公共汽车的位置如证据照片1所示。

随后，研讯休庭，直至周四上午10时继续。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
MAY 19 1939
Inquest on Mr. Bertram Lillie
Resumed
40296

Chinese Bus Conductress Gives Evidence ; Police
Officers Relate Their Stories

THE inquest on the body of the late Mr. Bertram Lillie, B.Sc.
Eng. (Lond), A.M.I.C.E., A.M.I.E., Principal of the Lester
School and Henry Lester Institute of Technical Education, who
was killed shortly after 9 p.m. on April 24 as the result of a
collision between his car and a Japanese-owned bus on Broadway,
near Minghong Road, was resumed yesterday by Mr. C. H. Haines,
H. M. Coroner in H.M. Police Court. After five witnesses, includ-
ing the Chinese conductress of the bus involved in the accident,
had given their evidence, the enquiry was adjourned until Monday
afternoon at 2.15 p.m. when it is expected that Mrs. Lillie will
give evidence.

Present at the inquest were
several Japanese officials representing
the Japanese Naval Landing Party
and others, while two Japanese re-
corded the evidence. Mr. R. R. C.
Master appeared on behalf of Mrs
Lillie and the Henry Lester Trustee
while also present was Mr. H. H.
Thomas, H.M Consul for Japanese
Affairs.

The first witness, Detective-Sergeant
Stanley Shaw Knowles, Crime Branch,
Police Headquarter testified that
seven photographs (produced) were
taken in his presence and under his
supervision on April 24 at 10 p.m.
on Broadway, near Minghong Road.
An eighth photograph was taken
under his supervision at Hongkong
Police Station.

Foreign Probationary Sergeant Al-
fred Raymond Turner, Traffic Branch,
Police Headquar ers, identified a plan
which had been drawn by himself
from measurements made by him-
self on the night of April 24 on
Broadway, east of Minghong Road.
This plan, he stated, represented the
position of a motor omnibus and a
motor car which had been involved
in a collision. He identified the two
vehicles from the photograph ex-
hibits.

Stopped by Marines

The next witness, Foreign Sergeant
E. V. Yablonsky, attached to Hong-
kew Police Station, told the Coroner
that at about 9.12 p.m. on April 24,
he went to Broadway, near Minghong
Road, in company with Chinese De-
tective-Sergeant 33, where he saw
two foreign males lying on stretchers
on the pavement, near a Fire Brigade
ambulance, and a foreign lady, who
was bleeding from the face. Also
present at the scene were a motor
car, licence number 5593, and a
Japanese bus, licence number 814.
These two vehicles, he continued,
were about 300 yards from the Ming-
hong Road corner, the bus facing
east and the car facing west.

He added that he began to collect
information at the scene and had
made some notes, when he was pre-
vented from doing so by Japanese
marines. Witness then instructed the
Chinese sergeant to inform Hongkew
Police station and he instructed the
ambulance driver to take the injured
people to hospital. He added that
the Chinese conductress of the bus
approached him and he saw that her
face was bleeding so he placed her
in the ambulance with the other
three persons. At the General Hos-
pital the two males were seen by Dr.
Patrick, the lady being taken up-
stairs while the Chinese girl was
removed to the Lester Chinese
Hospital.

At this point the Coroner stated
that he would not ask about a con-
versation between witness and Mrs.
Lillie as evidence of that would be
given later. Sergeant Yablonsky
added that the road was wet and
rather slippery and he recognized the
two vehicles involved in the accident
from the photographs.

1939年5月19日
伯特伦·利利先生死因研讯
复庭
40296

中国公共汽车女售票员作证；警官讲述经过

昨日，皇家验尸官 C. H. Haines 先生在皇家警察法庭复庭，就已故伯特伦·利利先生（B.Sc. Eng. (Lond), A.M.I.C.E., A.M.I.E.，莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院校长）的死因进行研讯。利利先生于4月24日晚9点后不久，因其汽车与一辆日属公共汽车在靠近明宏路的百老汇路发生碰撞而身亡。在五名证人（包括事故涉及公共汽车的中国女售票员）作证后，研讯休庭，预计将于周一下午2时15分复庭，届时利利夫人预计将出庭作证。

出席研讯的有数名代表日本海军陆战队及其他部门的日本官员，另有两名日本人记录了证词。R. R. C. Master 先生代表利利夫人及亨利·莱斯特信托基金出庭，负责日本事务的英国领事 H. H. Thomas 先生亦在场。

第一位证人，警察总部刑事科警长 Stanley Shaw Knowles 作证称，4月24日晚10时，在靠近明宏路的百老汇路，七张（提交的）照片是在他在场并监督下拍摄的。第八张照片是在他在虹口警察局监督下拍摄的。

警察总部交通科外籍见习警长 Alfred Raymond Turner 辨认了一份由他自己根据4月24日晚在明宏路以东百老汇路实地测量绘制的平面图。他表示，该图代表了卷入碰撞的一辆机动公共汽车和一辆机动车的位置。他从证据照片中辨认出了这两辆车。

被海军陆战队员制止

下一位证人，隶属虹口警察局的外籍警长 E. V. Yablonsky 告诉验尸官，4月24日晚9点12分左右，他与华探33号一同前往靠近明宏路的百老汇路，在那里他看到两名外籍男子躺在担架上，位于人行道上，靠近一辆消防队救护车，还有一名外籍女士，面部流血。现场还有一辆牌照号为5593的汽车和一辆牌照号为814的日本公共汽车。他继续说道，这两辆车距离明宏路路口约300码，公共汽车朝东，汽车朝西。

他补充说，他开始在现场收集信息并做了一些笔记，但被日本海军陆战队员阻止。证人随后指示华探通知虹口警察局，并指示救护车司机将伤者送往医院。他补充说，公共汽车的中国女售票员走近他，他看到她面部流血，于是将她与其他三人一起安置在救护车上。在广慈医院（General Hospital），两名男子由 Patrick 医生诊治，女士被带上楼，而那名中国女孩则被送往莱斯特华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。

此时，验尸官表示，他不会询问证人与利利夫人之间的谈话，因为相关证词稍后将提供。Yablonsky 警长补充说，路面潮湿且相当滑腻，他从照片中认出了事故涉及的两辆车。

R
19/5

pages.en:
Car Damaged

After questioning by Mr. Master,
he stated that the foreign lady had
rushed in his direction from one
of the stretchers shouting "See, my
husband is dead." She informed wit-
ness that her name was Lillie. One
of the foreigners on the stretchers he
noticed was a member of the S.M.P.

and on looking at him he found that
he was Sergeant R. J. Wimsett. The
other foreigner in civilian clothes he
did not know.

Sergeant John MacDonald, of the
Seaforth Highlanders, stated that he
was on duty at Garden Bridge at 8.40
p.m. on April 24. At about this time
a Ford sedan, travelling North, drew
up outside the police hut on the
bridge and he noticed that the right
headlamp and the mascot on the
bonnet were damaged. An English
woman and a man alighted from the
car and reported to the Foreign
S.M.P. Sergeant there that they had
been involved in an accident. The
lady pointed out the damage to the
car and requested the Foreign police
officer to accompany her so that she
could point out to him where the
accident had happened.

The police officer, witness stated,
got in the rear of the car, with the
man driving, and drove over the
bridge into the Japanese-occupied
area. About half an hour later, he
continued, a foreigner living at 1006
Avenue Joffre reported to him that
there had been a motor car accident
involving four or five American
citizens. Witness thereupon informed
a Japanese S.M.P. officer on duty at
the bridge and the latter told the
Japanese Naval Landing Party of the
accident. With the assistance of two
C.P.C.s witness then telephoned to
Central Police Station and informed
them of the accident.

"Knocked Unconscious"

The Chinese conductress of the
bus, who resides at Kwangsing Road,
opposite the Shanghai Cotton Mill,
said that the vehicle was owned by
the Wah Tsun Company which was
a Japanese and Chinese firm. "Did
anything happen to your bus last
month?" the Coroner asked the wit-
ness, who had been seated with the
Japanese officials attending the in-
quest, "No," she replied.

Mr. Haines—Nothing at all?
Witness—I don't know.

The Coroner then asked her if she
had been hurt last month and how
she had come by her injury. "Owing
to the collision of two cars," she
replied. One foreigner's car, she
said, had been involved in an accid-
ent with her bus about a month ago
on Broadway, near Minghong Road.
A Chinese was driving the bus and
of the vehicle when she was hurt,
she was selling tickets in the rear
Asked what had happened, she re-
plied that she did not see anything.

The Coroner—I did not ask you
what you saw I asked you what
happened.

Witness—I don't know.

The Coroner—How do you know
you were hurt?

Replying to the latter question the
conductress stated that she was un-
conscious after the collision. "Tell
this witness," Mr. Haines told the
interpreter, "that sometime ago, on
the same night, she was able to tell
the police in great detail what hap-
pened to her. Now she seems to
have forgotten. Would you remind
her?" Replying to this statement,
witness stated that she did not know
what she had told the police. She
added that she regained consciousness
after being taken to the hospital.

She added that she did not see the
bus collide with the car. The bus,
which had come from Garden Bridge,
was going along Broadway at a little
over 25 miles an hour. Asked how
she could estimate the speed of the
bus she replied that this was the
maximum speed allowed by the
company. It appeared to be going
slowly, she added. The enquiry was
then adjourned.

汽车受损

经马斯特先生（Mr. Master）讯问后，
他陈述称，那名外国女士从
其中一副担架处向他冲来，高喊：“看，我
丈夫死了。”她告知证
人她的名字是莉莉（Lillie）。他注
意到担架上的一名外国人系工部局警务处
（S.M.P.）成员。

他仔细查看后发现，
此人是 R. J. 温塞特（R. J. Wimsett）巡官。另一名身穿便服的外国人他不认识。

西福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的约翰·麦克唐纳（John MacDonald）巡官陈述称，4月24日晚8时40分，他在外白渡桥执勤。大约在此时，一辆向北行驶的福特轿车停在桥上的警亭外，他注意到右前大灯和引擎盖上的吉祥物饰物已损坏。一名英国妇女和一名男子从车上下来，向在场的外籍工部局警务处巡官报告称他们卷入了一起事故。该女士指出了车辆的损坏情况，并要求外籍警官随同她前往，以便向他指出事故发生地点。

证人陈述，该警官
坐进汽车后座，由那名男子驾驶，驾车过桥进入日军占领区。他继续说道，约半小时后，一名居住在霞飞路1006号的外国人向他报告称，发生了一起涉及四五名美国公民的汽车事故。证人随即通知了在桥上执勤的一名日籍工部局警务处警官，后者将此事故通报给了日本海军陆战队。随后，在两名中央捕房华捕（C.P.C.s）的协助下，证人致电中央捕房，向他们通报了该事故。

“昏迷不醒”

居住于广星路、上海棉纺厂对面的公交车女售票员表示，该车辆属于华纯公司（Wah Tsun Company），这是一家中日合资企业。“上个月你的公交车发生过什么事吗？”验尸官询问了当时与出席死因研讯的日本官员坐在一起的证人，“没有，”她回答。

海恩斯先生（Mr. Haines）——完全没有任何事？
证人——我不知道。

随后，验尸官询问她上个月是否受伤，以及是如何受伤的。“由于两车相撞，”她回答。她说，大约一个月前，在百老汇路靠近明宏路的地方，一名外国人的汽车与她的公交车发生了事故。当时是一名中国人在驾驶公交车，而她受伤时正在车厢后部售票。当被问及发生了什么时，她回答说她没有看到任何东西。

验尸官——我没有问你看到了什么，我问你发生了什么事。

证人——我不知道。

验尸官——你怎么知道你受伤了？

针对后一个问题，女售票员陈述称，碰撞后她失去了知觉。“告诉这位证人，”海恩斯先生对翻译说，“不久前，在同一天晚上，她能够非常详细地向警方讲述发生在她身上的事情。现在她似乎忘记了。你能提醒她一下吗？”对此陈述，证人回答说她不记得自己曾向警方说过什么。她补充说，被送往医院后她恢复了知觉。

她还补充说，她没有看到公交车与汽车相撞。这辆从外白渡桥驶来的公交车正以略高于每小时25英里的速度沿百老汇路行驶。当被问及她如何估算公交车的速度时，她回答说这是公司允许的最高速度。她补充说，车子看起来开得很慢。随后，研讯休庭。

MAY 18 1939

Japanese Prevented SMP
Inquiry At Lillie Crash

Story Told

Bus Conductress Says

Japanese marines prevented
him from obtaining informa-
tion from the driver of the bus
which smashed into Mr. Ber-
tram Lillie's car on April 24,
revealed Sergeant Yablonsky
of the SMP, attached to Hong-
kew station, at the inquest
into the death of Mr. Lillie,
resumed this morning at HBM
court, with Mr. C. H. Haines
acting as Coroner.

Yablonsky testified that he had
been ordered to the scene of the
accident about 9.12 p.m. on April
24. and that when he arrived
there he saw a motor bus, num-
ber 814, and a motor car, number
5593, which had been involved
in a collision, on Broadway, about
300 yards from Minghong Road.

Two Foreigners

"I saw two foreigners lying on
stretchers on the pavement" said
the police sergeant "and a for-
eign lady, bleeding from the face,
who rushed towards me crying
'See, my husband is dead'". Ser-
geant Yablonsky took charge of
the injured foreigners and
placed them in an ambulance,
conveying them to the General
Hospital. The Chinese conduct-
ress of the bus, who also appear-
ed to be injured about the face,
was taken in the ambulance to
the Lester hospital.

In all, five witnesses testified
in court this morning, the only
one who had been actually pre-
sent when the accident occurred
being the Chinese bus conductress.
Watching the case on behalf of
the Lester Institute Trustees and
Mrs. Lillie, was Mr. R. F. C.
Master.

Remembers Lillie

The bus conductress, a young
Chinese girl named Wu Fa-mung,
revealed very little of the facts
surrounding the wreck in her
rather halting and shy testi-
mony. She said that she had
been injured in the accident and
that she became unconscious,
stressing this point several times.
When questioned as to the speed
of the bus at the time of the
accident, she said that it was go-
ing a "little over 25 miles an
hour".

Asked how she knew that the
speed was 25 miles per hour, she
replied that that was the
maximum speed at which the
company regulations permitted
their vehicles to travel. She
could remember nothing more
concerning the accident, save
that she had been in the rear of
the bus selling tickets when the
crash came and she was rendered
unconscious.

1939年5月18日

日本人阻止工部局警务处
调查莉莉车祸案

死因研讯
披露案情

公交车售票员口风甚紧；声称
昏迷不醒

虹口站所属工部局警务处（SMP）亚布隆斯基（Yablonsky）巡官在今日上午于英国驻华最高法院（HBM court）恢复进行的莉莉（Lillie）先生死因研讯上披露，日本海军陆战队阻止他从4月24日撞毁伯特伦·莉莉（Bertram Lillie）先生汽车的公交车司机处获取信息。验尸官由 C. H. 海恩斯（C. H. Haines）先生担任。

亚布隆斯基作证称，他于4月24日晚9时12分左右奉命前往事故现场。当他到达那里时，他在距离明宏路约300码的百老汇路上，看到了一辆车牌号为814的公共汽车和一辆车牌号为5593的机动车发生了碰撞。

两名外国人

“我看到两名外国人躺在人行道上的担架上，”这位警佐说，“还有一名面部流血的外国女士向我冲来，哭喊着‘看，我丈夫死了’。”亚布隆斯基巡官负责照料受伤的外国人，并将他们安置在救护车中，送往总医院。同样面部似乎受伤的公交车中国女售票员也被救护车送往雷士德医院（Lester hospital）。

今天上午共有五名证人在法庭作证，其中唯一在事故发生时实际在场的是中国公交车女售票员。代表雷士德工学院托管人委员会及莉莉夫人观察此案的是 R. F. C. 马斯特（R. F. C. Master）先生。

记得莉莉

这位名叫吴法梦（Wu Fa-mung，音译）的年轻中国女售票员在其略显迟疑和害羞的证词中，几乎未透露围绕这起车祸的任何事实。她说她在事故中受伤并失去了知觉，多次强调这一点。当被问及事故发生时公交车的速度时，她说车速“略高于每小时25英里”。

当被问及她如何知道速度是每小时25英里时，她回答说那是公司规定允许车辆行驶的最高速度。除了车祸发生时她正在公交车后部售票并因此昏迷外，她对事故记不起更多情况。

Other Witnesses
Sergeant Yablonsky had previously testified that while he was at the scene of the wreck preparing to remove the injured, the bus conductress had approached him, her face bleeding, and informed him that she was hurt, getting into the ambulance and proceeding to the hospital. Said the conductress: "I don't remember what I told the policeman; I was unconscious".
The other witnesses who appeared this morning were Detective Sergeant Knowles of Crime Branch Headquarters, who supervised the photographing of the accident; Probationary Sergeant Turner of Traffic Headquarters, who drew the plan of the scene of the mishap; and Sergeant McDonald of the Seaforth Highlanders, who had been on duty at Garden Bridge at the time of the accident.
The inquest was adjourned until 2.15 next Monday afternoon, when five more witnesses are due to testify. It is doubtful that Mrs. Lillie will be able to testify next Monday.

其他证人
亚布隆斯基巡官此前曾作证称，当他在车祸现场准备移走伤者时，公交车女售票员走向他，面部流血，告知他自己受了伤，随后登上救护车前往医院。女售票员说：“我不记得我对警察说了什么；我当时昏迷了”。
今天上午出庭的其他证人包括：刑事总部侦缉巡官诺尔斯（Knowles），他负责监督事故现场拍照；交通总部试用巡官特纳（Turner），他绘制了事故现场图；以及西福斯高地团的麦克唐纳（McDonald）巡官，事故发生时他正在外白渡桥执勤。

High Tribute Paid To Late
Mr. Bertram Lillie

Man Of Outstanding Educational Achievement
And Ability; Shanghai Has Lost Figure Of
Importance In Engineering Activities

(Contributed)

The terrible tragedy which occurred on Monday night has deprived the youth of Shanghai of the services of a man of outstanding personality in the engineering and educational world. During the brief period that he has been resident in this city he has placed to his credit an achievement that many might consider a fitting monument to the work of a life time.

Prior to the arrival of Mr. Bertram Lillie in 1933 there had been a wide-spread realization of the unsuitability of much of the education that had been made available for Chinese students since the beginning of the century. The influence of western education had resulted in the creation and development of schools and colleges which failed to meet the needs of this present age and numbers of students were being graduated yearly for whom there was a lack of suitable work and little opportunity of any satisfactory career. Vocational education had been neglected and there were few, if any, institutions to supply training necessary to meet the demands of industrial and engineering development. This was especially evident in the large centres of population where scientific and industrial development had created an urgent demand for technically trained people. It had become obvious that education must, without delay, be brought into closer relationship to the industrial and commercial occupations of the people in order to bridge the gulf between the masses on the one hand and the more highly educated on the other hand.

Abundant Energy

The generous bequests of Mr. Henry Lester provided Mr. Lillie with a task for which he was eminently well fitted. His abundant energy, vitality and vigorous personality were such as enabled him to overcome all difficulties. In an amazingly short time after his arrival in Shanghai the local situation had been thoroughly surveyed, the advice and opinions of experienced engineers and educationists obtained, the needs estimated and the plans for the necessary building well under way. Mr. Lillie then returned to England where he made a tour of inspection, visiting all the important technical colleges in the country.

With that thoroughness which was so characteristic of him he investigated down to the smallest detail the methods and equipment in use and obtained all possible information as to the latest ideas and improvements in technical education. Following this he got into touch with the manufacturers of engineering and educational equipment and placed all the necessary orders for the Institute in Shanghai. At the same time he engaged the nucleus of a staff for the college.

Upon his return to Shanghai, at first from an office in the Medical Institute and later from the one room then available in the new building—Mr. Lillie began his work of supervising the erection of the building and the arrangement of courses of study for the day and evening classes. His energy, enthusiasm and driving power, ably supported by the newly arrived members of his staff, contributed greatly to the rapid completion of the plans.

Most Modern Lines

The classes commenced work on the most modern lines in the new building, the lay out and equipment of which evoked general admiration, seven months after the laying of the foundation stone. The first technical evening classes to be held in China began work the month following.

In 1936 the new extension was completed and officially opened by Sir Hughe Knatchbull-Hugessen in June 1937.

Mr. Lillie's efforts had resulted in an achievement of the highest order and his wonderful power of organization and efficient methods received praise from all quarters.

Numbers who enter the engineering world find that they are merely additions to a vast group who all have similar knowledge and experience and the most they can expect to earn is a living wage. Mr. Lillie, knowing how essential it is to hold a recognized engineering qualification or some similar proof of a thorough technical training, at once began the task of raising the status of the institute and gaining recognition for its graduates. He maintained close touch with government educational circles, making many visits to Nanking, and finally obtained the approval of the Board of Education for the diplomas issued by the Lester Institute. Not content with this he opened negotiations with the University of London in an endeavour to obtain recognition of the Lester Institute as a University College. His last visit to England was in connection with these proposals and there was every prospect that his untiring efforts were about to be crowned with success.

高度赞誉已故
伯特伦·莉莉先生

一位在教育成就和能力方面杰出的人士；上海失去了一位在工程活动中具有重要地位的人物

（投稿）

周一晚间发生的可怕悲剧，使上海青年失去了一位在工程和教育界具有杰出人格魅力的人士的服务。在他居住于本市的短暂期间，他所取得的成就足以被视为其毕生工作的合适纪念碑，这是许多人都会认可的。

在伯特伦·莉莉先生于1933年到来之前，人们已广泛认识到，自本世纪初以来为中国学生提供的许多教育并不适宜。西方教育的影响导致了一些学校和学院的建立与发展，但这些学校未能满足当今时代的需求，每年都有大量毕业生毕业，却缺乏合适的工作机会，也鲜有获得满意职业生涯的机会。职业教育受到忽视，几乎没有机构能够提供满足工业和工程发展需求的必要培训。这在人口密集的大中心尤为明显，科学和工业的发展创造了对技术训练人员的迫切需求。显而易见，必须毫不拖延地使教育与人民的工商业职业更紧密地联系起来，以弥合大众与受过高等教育者之间的鸿沟。

充沛的精力

亨利·雷士德（Henry Lester）先生的慷慨遗赠为莉莉先生提供了一项他极其胜任的任务。他充沛的精力、活力和刚毅的个性使他能够克服所有困难。在他抵达上海后的极短时间内，当地情况得到了彻底调查，获得了经验丰富的工程师和教育家的建议与意见，评估了需求，并且必要建筑的计划已顺利展开。随后，莉莉先生返回英国，进行了一次视察之旅，走访了该国所有重要的技术学院。

他以一贯的细致作风，深入调查了使用中方法和设备的每一个细节，并获取了关于技术教育最新理念和改进的所有可能信息。此后，他与工程和教学设备制造商取得联系，并为上海的学院下达了所有必要的订单。同时，他为学院聘请了核心教职员工。

回到上海后，莉莉先生起初在医学院的一间办公室工作，后来在新大楼当时可用的一间房间里工作，开始监督大楼的建造以及日间和夜间课程的学习安排。他的精力、热情和驱动力，在新到任的教职员工的有力支持下，极大地促进了计划的迅速完成。

最现代化的路线

在奠基七个月后，课程在新大楼中以最现代化的方式开始运作，其布局和装备赢得了普遍的赞赏。中国首批技术夜校班次于次月开始上课。

1936年，新扩建部分完工，并于1937年6月由休·纳奇布尔-赫格森爵士（Sir Hughe Knatchbull-Hugessen）正式揭幕。

莉莉先生的努力取得了最高水平的成就，他出色的组织能力和高效的方法受到了各方的赞扬。

许多进入工程界的人发现，他们只是庞大群体中的新增成员，所有人都拥有类似的知识和经验，他们最多只能期望赚取维持生活的工资。莉莉先生深知持有公认的工程资格或某种类似的全方位技术培训证明至关重要，立即着手提高学院的地位并为其毕业生争取认可。他与政府教育界保持密切联系，多次访问南京，最终获得了教育部对雷士德工学院颁发文凭的认可。他并不满足于此，又与伦敦大学展开谈判，试图使雷士德工学院获得作为大学学院的认可。他最后一次访问英国即与此提议有关，而他不懈的努力即将取得成功的前景十分广阔。

Outside Activity

In spite of his arduous duties in
connection with the School and
Institute Mr. Lillie found time for
a considerable measure of outside
activity. He was convinced that en-
gineering should rank high among
the professions. No one realized
more clearly than Mr. Lillie that
the engineer of the future must be
trained to deal with men as well
as with machines, that he must cul-
tivate human interests and associa-
tions, that he must take every oppor-
tunity to further personal and busi-
ness relations, and should be pre-
pared to shoulder the burdens of
public affairs.

From the time of his arrival he
closely associated himself with the
work of the Engineering Society of
China of which he became Vice-
President. He was Chairman of the
Apprenticeship Committee and also
of the Technical Education Com-
mittee of that Society. By placing
the College Hall and Library at the
disposal of the Society and by
founding a Students' Engineering
Society he enlisted the support and
interest of the members of the par-
ent body.

Mr. Lillie was also Secretary of
the Shanghai Association of the In-
stitution of Civil Engineers, a Mem-
ber of the Scholarship Committee of
the Federation of British Indus-
tries and a Member of the Com-
mittee of the Cathedral School,
Henry Lester Endowment. He dis-
played great interest in the work of
the Foundations Research Commit-
tee and also in Commercial Testing,
maintaining close relations with
many industrial concerns.

In this untimely manner has end-
ed the life of a man of high educa-
tional attainment whose excellent
work, especially during the last six
years, gave promise of even greater
things to come. His loss will be
deplored by all who came into con-
tact with him and above all by the
students, on whose behalf he had
exerted himself to the fullest ex-
tent.

校外活动

尽管利里（Lillie）先生在学校及学院的事务中肩负着繁重的职责，但他仍抽出时间参与了大量的校外活动。他深信，工程学应在各类职业中占据崇高地位。没有人比利里先生更清楚地认识到，未来的工程师必须接受训练，不仅要懂得操作机器，还要善于与人打交道；他必须培养对人事务的兴趣并建立社会联系；他必须抓住一切机会增进个人及业务关系，并准备好承担公共事务的重担。

自抵达上海之日起，他便紧密参与中国工程学会（Engineering Society of China）的工作，并担任该会副会长。他还担任该会学徒委员会及技术教育委员会的主席。通过将学院礼堂和图书馆供该会使用，并创立学生工程学会，他赢得了母体组织成员的支持与关注。

利里先生还担任英国土木工程师学会上海分会秘书、英国工业联合会奖学金委员会委员，以及亨利·雷士德捐赠基金大教堂学校委员会委员。他对基金会研究委员会的工作以及商业测试表现出浓厚兴趣，并与许多工业企业保持着密切关系。

一位拥有高深教育造诣的人士就这样过早地结束了生命。他的出色工作，尤其是在过去六年中的表现，预示着未来将取得更大的成就。所有与他接触过的人，尤其是那些他曾为之竭尽全力的学生们，都将对他的离世深感痛惜。

training, at once began the task of
raising the status of the institute
and gaining recognition for its
graduates. He maintained close
touch with government educational
circles, making many visits to Nan-
king, and finally obtained the ap-
proval of the Board of Education
for the diplomas issued by the
Lester Institute.
"Not content with this Mr. Lillie
opened negotiations with Uni-
versity of London in an endeavor
to obtain recognition of the Lester
Institute as a University College.
His last visit to England was in
connection with these proposals
and there was every prospect that
his untiring efforts were about to
be crowned with success.

Many Other Activities

"In spite of his arduous duties in
connection with the school and
institute Mr. Lillie found time for
a considerable measure of outside
activity.
"From the time of his arrival he
closely associated himself with the
work of the Engineering Society of
China of which he became vice-
president. He was Chairman of
the Apprenticeship Committee and
also of the Technical Education
Committee of that society. By plac-
ing the College Hall and library at
the disposal of the society and by
founding a Students' Engineering
Society he enlisted the support and
interest of the members of the
parent body.
pages.zh:
“随后，利里先生返回英国，进行了一次视察之旅，走访了该国所有重要的技术学院。他以一贯的彻底精神，对使用中的方法和设备进行了细致入微的调查，并获取了关于技术教育最新理念和改进的所有可能信息。

“此后，他与工程及教育设备制造商取得联系，并为上海的学院下达了所有必要的订单。同时，他为学院聘请了核心教职员工。

监督建筑

“回到上海后，利里先生起初在医学院的一间办公室办公，后来在新大楼当时唯一可用的一间房间里办公，开始监督大楼的建造以及日间和夜间课程的教学安排。他的精力、热情和驱动力，在新到任的教职员工的得力支持下，极大地促进了计划的迅速完成。

“奠基七个月后，课程在新大楼中按照最现代化的方式开始运作，其布局和设备赢得了普遍的赞赏。中国首批技术夜校班次于次月开始上课。

“1936年，新扩建部分完工，并于1937年6月由许阁森爵士（Sir Hughe Knatchbull-Hugessen）正式揭幕。

“利里先生的努力促成了一项最高等级的成就，他出色的组织能力和高效的方法受到了各方的赞扬。

提升地位

“利里先生深知持有公认的工程资格或某种类似的全方位技术培训证明至关重要，因此立即着手提升学院的地位，并为其毕业生争取认可。他与政府教育界保持密切联系，多次前往南京，最终获得了教育部对雷士德学院颁发文凭的批准。

“利里先生并不满足于此，他又与伦敦大学展开谈判，试图使雷士德学院被认可为大学学院。他最后一次访问英国即与此提案有关，且有充分迹象表明，他不懈的努力即将获得成功。

众多其他活动

“尽管利里先生在学校和学院的事务中肩负着繁重的职责，但他仍抽出时间参与了大量的校外活动。

“自抵达之日起，他便紧密参与中国工程学会的工作，并担任该会副会长。他还担任该会学徒委员会及技术教育委员会的主席。通过将学院礼堂和图书馆供该会使用，并创立学生工程学会，他赢得了母体组织成员的支持与关注。

pages.en:
"Mr. Lillie was also Secretary of
the Shanghai Association of the
Institution of Civil Engineers, a
Member of the Scholarship Com-
mittee of the Federation of British
Industries and a Member of the
Committee of the Cathedral School,
Henry Lester Endowment. He dis-
played great interest in the work
of the Foundation's Research Com-
mittee and also in Commercial
Testing, maintaining close relations
with many industrial concerns.
"His untimely death ended the
life of a man of high educational
attainment whose excellent work,
especially during the last six years,
gave promise of even greater
things to come. His loss will be
deplored by all who came into con-
tact with him and above all by the
students, on whose behalf he had
exerted himself to the fullest ex-
tent," Mr. Lillie's colleague conclud-
ed.
pages.zh:
“利里先生还担任英国土木工程师学会上海分会秘书、英国工业联合会奖学金委员会委员，以及亨利·雷士德捐赠基金大教堂学校委员会委员。他对基金会研究委员会的工作以及商业测试表现出浓厚兴趣，并与许多工业企业保持着密切关系。

“他的过早离世结束了一位拥有高深教育造诣的人士的生命。他的出色工作，尤其是在过去六年中的表现，预示着未来将取得更大的成就。所有与他接触过的人，尤其是那些他曾为之竭尽全力的学生们，都将对他的离世深感痛惜，”利里先生的同事总结道。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 27 1939
Wimsett Does Not Remember
Anything Of Accident
Police Sergeant Suffering From After Effects
Of Concussion; Had Been Called At Garden
Bridge; Mrs. Lillie Not Questioned Yet
With Sergeant R. J. Wimsett suf-
fering from the after effects of
concussion as the result of injuries
sustained in the motor crash on
Monday night on Broadway, and
not remembering anything of the
accident, officers of the Shanghai
Municipal Police were not able to
proceed much further with their
inquiries into the circumstances
leading up to the fatal crash
The doctor attending Wimsett,
who had tried to question the in-
jured sergeant, stated that it was
not unusual in cases of this na-
ture for the patients to forget
everything immediately preceding
the accident. Sergeant Wimsett not
only does not remember anything
of the crash, according to reports,
but doesn't even remember getting
into the late Mr. Bertram Lillie's
car. The doctor is hopeful that
Sergeant Wimsett will get over
this condition in a short while and
will then be able to make a state-
ment.
Mrs. Lillie was still not sufficient-
ly in a fit condition yesterday to
make any statement to the police.
It was definitely ascertained yes-
terday that Sergeant Wimsett was
called by a foreign couple, appar-
ently Mr. and Mrs. Lillie, from the
Garden Bridge where he had been
on duty. He was standing near the
sentry box of the Seaforth High-
landers when he was called, ac-
cording to reports of witnesses, to
assist settling a traffic accident.
It was denied by a Japanese
Naval spokesman on Tuesday that
either Mr. or Mrs. Lillie had reach-
ed the Garden Bridge after having
allegedly dragged the barbed wire
barrier off the Hongkew Bridge.
Statements necessary for the
lodging of the protest with the
Japanese authorities for the alleg-
ed assault on Mr. A. H. Sampson,
Assistant Commissioner of the
S.M.P., were being prepared by
the S.M.P. yesterday. The state-
ments will be forwarded to the
Council, who will file the protest.
"No Reason For Protest"
At the press conference yester-
day afternoon, both the Embassy
spokesman and the Navy spokesman
said that no protest had yet been
received from either the Shanghai
Municipal Council or the Shang-
hai Municipal Police over the as-
sault on Mr. A. H. Samson, Assist-
ant Commissioner of Police, "C"
Division, by a Japanese naval
officer at the General Hospital.
"The naval spokesman does not
see any reason for a protest," said
the interpreter.
Funeral Arrangements
Funeral arrangements for Mr.
Lillie were announced yesterday.
Mr. Lillie will be buried at the
Bubbling Well Cemetery at 4
o'clock to-morrow afternoon. At
present the body is lying at the
International Funeral Directors.

《上海泰晤士报》（SHANGHAI TIMES）
1939年4月27日
温姆塞特不记得事故的任何情况
警长遭受脑震荡后遗症；曾在花园桥被传唤；利里夫人尚未接受问询

由于R. J. 温姆塞特（R. J. Wimsett）警长因周一晚在百老汇路发生的机动车撞车事故中受伤而遭受脑震荡后遗症，且不记得事故的任何情况，上海公共租界工部局警务处的警官们无法就导致这起致命车祸的情况进一步展开调查。

负责诊治温姆塞特的医生曾试图询问这位受伤的警长，他表示，在此类病例中，患者忘记事故发生前的一切情况并不罕见。据报道，温姆塞特警长不仅不记得撞车的任何情况，甚至不记得登上已故的伯特伦·利里先生的汽车。医生希望温姆塞特警长能在短时间内恢复此状况，届时他将能够作出陈述。

昨日，利里夫人的身体状况仍不足以向警方作出任何陈述。

昨日已确切查明，温姆塞特警长是在花园桥执勤时，被一对外籍夫妇（显然是利里夫妇）传唤过去的。据目击者称，当他被传唤去协助处理一起交通事故时，他正站在海福尔高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的岗亭附近。

周二，一位日本海军发言人否认了利里先生或利里夫人在 allegedly（据称）拖走虹口桥的铁丝网障碍物后到达花园桥的说法。

警务处昨日正在准备必要的陈述，以便就涉嫌袭击警务处助理处长A. H. 桑普森（A. H. Sampson）先生一事向日本当局提出抗议。这些陈述将提交给工部局，由工部局正式提出抗议。

“没有理由提出抗议”

在昨日下午的新闻发布会上，大使馆发言人和海军发言人均表示，尚未收到来自上海公共租界工部局或上海公共租界工部局警务处关于日本海军军官在总医院袭击警务处“C”区助理处长A. H. 桑普森先生的任何抗议。

翻译人员称：“海军发言人认为没有理由提出抗议。”

葬礼安排

昨日公布了利里先生的葬礼安排。利里先生将于明日下午4点安葬于静安寺公墓（Bubbling Well Cemetery）。目前，遗体停放在国际殡仪馆。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
APR 27 1939

S. M. C. to Study
Hospital Incident

Accident Victims Slowly
Improving ; Protest to
Japanese Likely

A detailed report on the incident
which occurred in the reception hall
of the General Hospital on the
evening of April 24, when Mr. A. H.
Samson, Assistant Commissioner of
the Shanghai Municipal Police, was
hit by a lieutenant of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, was expected
to be in the hands of the Secretary-
General of the Shanghai Municipal
Council some time this morning, it
was understood yesterday afternoon,
although no official confirmation
could be obtained.

The report, together with the
statements of witnesses will be
studied by the members of the
Council, with a view to ascertain
the actual circumstances of the
incident and according to the find-
ings of the Council, a protest may
be lodged with the Japanese Con-
sulate-General, it was learned.

The incident, it will be recalled,
occurred after Mrs. B. Lillie and
Sergt. R. J. Wimsett had been ad-
mitted to the hospital for treat-
ment of serious injuries sustained
during a motor car accident on
Broadway in which Mr. Bertram
Lillie, Principal of the Lester School
and Henry Lester Institute of
Technical Research, was killed.

Meanwhile, Mrs. Lillie was slight-
ly better yesterday, although doctors
attending her did not permit her
being questioned by the authorities,
regarding the accident. Mr. Wimsett,
who was operated upon for the
second time in two days yesterday
afternoon, was stated to be resting
comfortably last night and attending
physicians said that he was doing
as well as could be expected. Whilst
his condition is still serious, it was
understood that the doctors expected
to save his life, although Mr. Wim-
sett would be detained in hospital for
quite some time. He regained con-
sciousness late yesterday morning,
for the first time since the accident
and his condition does not permit
his being questioned as yet.

《字林西报》。
1939年4月27日

工部局将研究
医院事件

事故受害者病情缓慢
好转；可能向日本方面
提出抗议

据悉，关于4月24日晚在总医院接待大厅发生的一起事件的详细报告，预计将于今天上午某时送达上海公共租界工部局总干事手中。在该事件中，上海公共租界警务处助理总监 A. H. 萨姆森（A. H. Samson）先生遭到日本海军陆战队一名中尉的袭击。尽管昨日下午尚无法获得官方证实，但上述消息已为人所知。

据了解，工部局董事将结合证人陈述对该报告进行研究，以查明事件的实际经过。根据工部局的调查结果，可能会向日本总领事馆提出抗议。

回顾可知，该事件发生在 B. 利利（B. Lillie）夫人和 R. J. 温塞特（R. J. Wimsett）巡长因在百老汇路（Broadway）发生的车祸中受重伤而被送入医院接受治疗之后。在那场车祸中，雷士德学校及雷士德工学研究院院长伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie）先生不幸身亡。

与此同时，利利夫人昨日病情略有起色，但主治医生不允许当局就事故情况向她问话。温塞特巡长在昨日下午接受了两天内的第二次手术，据称昨晚休息状况良好，主治医生表示其恢复情况符合预期。虽然他的病情仍然严重，但据悉医生预计能保住他的生命，尽管温塞特先生将在医院滞留相当长一段时间。他在昨日上午晚些时候自事故发生以来首次恢复意识，但其身体状况目前仍不允许接受问话。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

APR 26 1939

Japanese Assault
Upon A.H. Samson
Reported To SMC

With all details collected, the
report of the assault on Mr. A. H.
Samson, Assistant Commissioner of
Police in charge of "C" Division
S.M.P., by an officer of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party at the Gen-
eral Hospital two nights ago, was
forwarded to the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council this morning. It is
expected that a strong protest will
be made. No apology has as yet
been made by the naval officer nor
his superiors.
Sergeant R. J. Wimsett and Mrs.
Bertram Lillie are still in no con-
dition to be interviewed, and no
statements can be taken from them
yet. Sergeant Wimsett is believed
to have lost his memory as the re-
sult of the concussion suffered in
the accident in which Mr. Bertram
Lillie was killed.
It is now believed that Sergeant
Wimsett accompanied Mr. Lillie
from the Garden Bridge, where he
was on duty, to help Mr. Lillie get
past sentries on Broadway bridge
who had previously turned him
back, but it may be several days
before a complete story of the
tragedy in which a Japanese bus
hit Mr. Lillie's car can be assem-
bled.

1939年4月26日

日本军官袭击
A.H. 萨姆森一事
已报告工部局

随着所有细节收集完毕，关于两日前在总医院发生的日本海军陆战队军官袭击上海公共租界警务处“C”区主管、助理总监 A. H. 萨姆森先生的报告，已于今晨呈送上海公共租界工部局。预计将会提出强烈抗议。该海军军官及其上级至今尚未作出任何道歉。

R. J. 温塞特巡长和伯特伦·利利夫人目前仍不适合接受问询，因此尚无法从他们那里获取陈述。据信，温塞特巡长因在导致伯特伦·利利先生死亡的车祸中遭受脑震荡而失忆。

目前认为，温塞特巡长当时正执勤于外白渡桥（Garden Bridge），他陪同利利先生前往，旨在帮助利利先生通过此前曾将其折返的百老汇路桥哨兵。但要拼凑出这起悲剧的完整经过——即一辆日本巴士撞击利利先生汽车的事件——可能还需要数天时间。

Wimsett Injury
Remains Serious

Details Of Fatal Auto
Smash Awaited

With the two witnesses still
unable to talk, the complete de-
tails of the auto smash which last
night killed Mr. Bertram Lillie,

hai Municipal Police The two

INQUEST OPENS
H.B.M. Registrar, sitting as
Coroner, opened the inquest on
the death of Mr. Bertram Lillie
today at 2.30 p.m., at the premises
of the International Funeral
Directors, where formal evidence
of identification was given.

are Mrs. Lillie, who this morning
showed some improvement, and
Sergeant R. J. Wimsett of the
SMP, whose condition is still
serious.
The three were in Mr. Lillie's
car at 9 o'clock last night, when a
Japanese sentry jumped onto the
running board on Broadway, and
the car struck, near Boone Road,
one of the pirate buses run by
the Japanese without SMC license,
in violation of the China General
Omnibus Co. franchise, and with
only tiny blue running lights
which are difficult to see at night.
Mr. Lillie, at the wheel, was killed
instantly, and the other two, to-
gether with the sentry, injured.

A. H. Samson Assaulted
At the General Hospital an of-
ficer of the Japanese Naval Land-
ing Party accompanied by two
guards attempted to butt into the
affair, tried to get into the operat-
ing theatre and, when he found
that Mr. A. H. Samson, Assistant

stand him, hit Mr. Samson below
the right ear with his fist and
ordered him out of the building.
No apology for the unwarranted
assault has as yet been made to

this morning. He added that the
police were busy collecting all de-
tails of the affair, which may
take a little time owing to the
condition of Mrs. Lillie and Sgt.
Wimsett, and will forward a
complete report to the council.

whether a protest has been made
to the Japanese elicited the reply
that the Council were still await-
ing details, which are obviously
not available yet.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
1939年4月25日

温塞特伤情
仍然严重

工部局等待
致命车祸详情

由于两名证人仍无法开口说话，上海公共租界警务处尚无法查明昨晚导致雷士德学校及雷士德工学院院长、理学学士（伦敦）、英国土木工程师学会会员、机械工程师学会会员伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie, BSc FNG (London), AMICE, AMIME）先生死亡的车祸的全部细节。这两名证人是利利夫人，她今晨病情略有好转；以及警务处 R. J. 温塞特巡长，其病情仍然严重。

验尸开庭
英国驻华女王陛下注册官担任验尸官，于今日下午2时30分在国际殡仪馆 premises 开启对伯特伦·利利先生死因的研讯，并在会上进行了正式的身份确认举证。

昨晚9时，三人同在利利先生的车内。此时，一名日本哨兵跳上百老汇路上的汽车踏板，随后该车在布恩路（Boone Road）附近撞上了一辆由日本人运营、无工部局执照、违反中国公共汽车公司专营权、且仅装有夜间难以看清的微小蓝色行车灯的“海盗巴士”。驾驶汽车的利利先生当场死亡，另外两人连同那名哨兵受伤。

A. H. 萨姆森遭袭
在总医院，一名日本海军陆战队军官在两名卫兵陪同下试图强行介入此事，企图进入手术室。当他发现警察助理总监 A. H. 萨姆森先生不懂足够的日语以理解其意图时，便用拳头击打萨姆森先生右耳下方，并命令他离开大楼。一位高级官员今晨表示，警方尚未就这一无理袭击行为收到任何道歉。他补充说，警方正忙于收集此事的所有细节，鉴于利利夫人和温塞特巡长的状况，这可能需要一点时间，随后将向工部局提交完整报告。向秘书处查询是否已向日本方面提出抗议时，得到的答复是工部局仍在等待详情，而这些详情显然目前尚不可得。

（印：档案）
（批：C 80/4）

pages.en:
House Robbed
Mr. Lillie, a brilliant education-
alist who was the organizer of the
Lester Institute, had only just re-
turned two days ago from a trip
to England, which he made in
order to engage a professor of
mathematics. Mrs. Lillie did not
accompany him, but remained in
Shanghai with her three-year old
daughter.
The SMP had been awaiting
the return of Mr. Lillie, as during
his absence his home at 401 Great
Western Road had been burgled,
and thousands of dollars worth of
property taken including a radio-
gramaphone valued at 400. Mrs.
Lillie could not state the exact
value of the goods taken, and the
detectives were waiting to question
Mr. Lillie on this subject. The
robbery was one of many recent
ones in this district, where houses
have their fronts on municipal
roads and their backs in badlands
territory unpatrolled by the SMP.
pages.zh:
住宅遭窃
利利先生是一位杰出的教育家，也是雷士德研究院的组织者。他两天前刚从英国旅行归来，此行目的是聘请一位数学教授。利利夫人并未随行，而是留在上海陪伴其三岁的女儿。

上海公共租界警务处一直在等待利利先生归来，因为在他外出期间，其位于大西路401号的寓所遭窃，价值数千美元的财物被盗，其中包括一台价值400美元的无线电留声机。利利夫人无法说明被盗物品的确切价值，侦探们正等待就此事项询问利利先生。此次抢劫是该地区近期多起抢劫案中的一起，这些地区的房屋前门面向市政道路，而后门则位于警务处未巡逻的“坏地”（badlands）区域。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

1939
Inquest on Mr. Bertram Lillie
Opened by H.M. Coroner

Condition of Sergeant Wimsett, Mrs. Lillie Still
Serious ; Questions Over Hospital Incident

THE inquest on the body of Mr. Bertram Lillie, B. Sc. Eng.
(Lond), A.M.I.C.E., A.M.I.E., Principal of the Lester School and
Henry Lester Institute of Technical Education, who was killed
shortly after 9 p.m. on Monday evening as the result of a collision
between his car and a Japanese-operated bus on Broadway, near
Boone Road, was opened yesterday by Mr. I. T. Morris, Acting
H. M. Coroner, at the Parlours of the International Funeral Direc-
tors on Kiaochow Road, where the body had been conveyed from
the General Hospital. The condition of Mrs. Lillie and of Sergeant
R. J. Wimsett, of the Shanghai Municipal Police, both of whom
were passengers in the car at the time of the accident, was stated
to be still serious yesterday. Sergeant Wimsett was still uncon-
scious following his multiple injuries, which included a fractured
left leg (broken in two places), a broken clavicle, gashes on the
forehead and a broken nose, while Mrs. Lillie was stated to be
suffering from severe nervous shock. Both the injured people
would not be able to answer questions for two or three days, it
was asserted.

The incident is at present under
investigation by the British authori-
ties in co-operation with the Muni-
cipal Police. Until after the inquest
has been closed and all the evidence
becomes available, including the
statements of Mrs. Lillie and Sergt.
Wimsett, the passengers in the car,
who stated that he had known Mr.
Lillie for the past six years. He had
last seen him alive at 5 p.m. on
Monday at the Institute, 505 East
Seward Road. The enquiry was ad-
journed sine die.

A Japanese sailor named Igarashi,
who was severely injured during the
impact between the bus and the car
as he was standing on the running
board of the latter vehicle, died in
hospital yesterday morning. The
bus, the Japanese authorities re-
vealed yesterday, was owned by the
Kechu Bus Company and was driven
by an employee named Wu Mao-
fung.

At the Japanese press conference
last night a Navy spokesman stated
that he had visited the scene of the
accident on Monday night. At about
9.20 p.m., he went on, a car was pro-
ceeding from East to West, crossing
Broadway Bridge over Hongkew
Creek. In so doing, he stated, it hit
a barbed wire barricade on the
bridge. It did not stop and continued
westwards, he alleged.

Dragging Barricade

"The sentry on duty there," con-
tinued the spokesman, "shouted
'Stop' to the driver in English, but
the car did not take any heed and
continued for about 100 metres, when
an S.M.P. member on duty there
signalled the vehicle to stop. The
car stopped," he continued, "at a
point on the intersection of Boone
Road and Broadway, still dragging
the barricade."

The S.M.P. member in question
then boarded the car, which returned
to the bridge, he went on. At the
time there was a Briton driving the
car and a lady sat beside him.
Continuing with his statement, the
spokesman said that the car proceed-
ed past the remaining barricade and
turned round. The sentry, through
a Japanese civilian who had a
knowledge of English, then tried to
ascertain the reason why the car
had not stopped previously.

"At that time the S.M.P. sergeant
was in the car, and the driver, paying
no heed to the questions, started the
vehicle and went towards the west,
the sentry on the north side of the
bridge jumping on the running board
in an effort to stop the car," the
spokesman continued.

"Zig-Zag Fashion"

"The lady in the car shouted
'Stop,' but the driver continued west
at a high rate of speed, driving in
a zig-zag fashion across the road as
if he was attempting to shake the
sentry off the running board," the
spokesman alleged. Near the corner
of Nanzing Road and Broadway this
car ran into a bus that was proceed-
ing eastwards on the north side of
the street and on the right hand side
of the car, he further stated.

As a result of the collision the
driver of the car was killed, and
the sentry on the running board was
severely injured, being jammed be-
tween the two vehicles. As a result
of his injuries he had died the fol-
lowing morning, while the lady and
the S.M.P. member were wounded,
the spokesman concluded. Investiga-
tions, he added, were still being
continued by the Japanese Military
Police and the Japanese Special
Naval Landing Party.

《字林西报》，

1939年
英国驻华女王陛下验尸官开启
对伯特伦·利利先生的死因研讯

温塞特巡长、利利夫人病情仍然
严重；医院事件引发疑问

针对雷士德学校及雷士德工学院院长、理学学士（工程）（伦敦）、英国土木工程师学会会员、机械工程师学会会员伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie, B. Sc. Eng. (Lond), A.M.I.C.E., A.M.I.E.）先生遗体的死因研讯，于昨日由代理英国驻华女王陛下验尸官 I. T. 莫里斯（I. T. Morris）先生开启。利利先生于周一晚9点后不久，因其汽车在百老汇路近布恩路处与一辆日本运营的巴士相撞而身亡。遗体已从总医院运至胶州路国际殡仪馆礼堂。据悉，车祸发生时同在车内的乘客、上海公共租界警务处 R. J. 温塞特巡长和利利夫人，昨日病情仍然严重。温塞特巡长在多处受伤后仍处于昏迷状态，伤势包括左腿两处骨折、锁骨断裂、额头割伤以及鼻梁骨折；而利利夫人据称遭受严重的神经休克。据称，两名伤者将在两三天内无法回答问题。

该事件目前正由英国当局与警务处合作调查。在研讯结束且所有证据（包括车内乘客利利夫人和温塞特巡长的陈述）齐备之前，调查将持续进行。温塞特巡长表示认识利利先生已有六年。他最后一次见到活着的利利先生是在周一下午5点，地点位于东熙华德路505号的研究院。研讯无限期休庭。

一名名叫五十岚（Igarashi）的日本水兵，在巴士与汽车相撞时因站在后者踏板上而受重伤，于昨日上午在医院去世。日本当局昨日透露，该巴士属于协中巴士公司（Kechu Bus Company），由一名名叫吴茂峰（Wu Mao-fung，音译）的员工驾驶。

在昨晚的日本记者招待会上，一位海军发言人表示，他曾在周一晚视察事故现场。他接着说，大约晚上9点20分，一辆汽车由东向西行驶，穿过虹口港上的百老汇路桥。在此过程中，他说，汽车撞上了桥上的一道铁丝网路障。据称，汽车并未停下，而是继续向西行驶。

拖拽路障

发言人继续说道：“当时执勤的哨兵用英语向司机大喊‘停车’，但汽车未予理会，继续行驶了约100米，此时一名在此执勤的警务处成员示意车辆停止。”他接着说，“汽车停在布恩路与百老汇路交叉口的某处，仍然拖拽着路障。”

他说，随后该名警务处成员登上汽车，汽车返回桥上。当时开车的是英国人，旁边坐着一位女士。发言人继续陈述称，汽车驶过剩余的路障并掉头。随后，哨兵通过一名懂英语的日本平民，试图查明汽车此前为何不停车。

“当时警务处巡长在车内，司机无视提问，启动车辆向西驶去，桥北侧的哨兵跳上踏板，试图阻止汽车，”发言人继续说道。

“之字形行驶”

“车内的女士大喊‘停车’，但司机继续高速向西行驶，在道路上呈之字形驾驶，仿佛试图将哨兵从踏板上甩下，”发言人声称。他进一步指出，在南京路与百老汇路拐角附近，这辆汽车撞上了一辆在街道北侧、汽车右侧向东行驶的巴士。

发言人总结道，碰撞结果导致汽车司机死亡，踏板上的哨兵被夹在两车之间受重伤。哨兵因伤势于次日早晨死亡，而女士和警务处成员受伤。他补充说，日本宪兵队和日本特别海军陆战队仍在继续进行调查。

档案
（批：警务处长致副总监（特务科） 4月26日）

Lillie at the British Court, the

Police Enquiries

Asked if the police were permitted
free access to the wreckage of the
two vehicles, as they were not at
Hongkew Police Station, the spokes-
man said that the Municipal Police
had already ended their investigations
when Commdr. Mitsonobu arrived on

the sentry.

a pressman, who enquired if the bar-

lights according to Traffic Regulations.
"There was ample light to show these
barricades," he added.

Hospital Incident

Referring to events later at the
General Hospital when a Japanese
naval officer was stated by eye-
witnesses to have arrived there, ac-
companied by two sailors with fixed
bayonets, and to have strode up and
down the Reception Hall giving
orders in Japanese, insisting to be
shown to the patients' room and the
doctors in charge, a correspondent
asked if any information had been
received in connection with the visit
of Japanese marines to the Hospital
where something of a "rumpus" had
been created.

随后，一名记者问道，利里（Lillie）先生是否确实已行至外白渡桥并被折返，这一说法是否正确。“他显然是从稍远于布恩路（Boone Road）的地方返回的，”发言人回答道。另一名记者问：“公共汽车是否撞上了那辆汽车？”发言人称：“发生了一起碰撞。”提问者进一步追问，公共汽车从后方撞击汽车是否属实。对此，发言人表示，该汽车呈之字形行驶，碰撞角度约为20度。他补充说，日本哨兵的颅骨被压碎，当时已无法回答任何问题。

针对一位询问者的提问——即事故现场的证人是否被允许在英国法庭对利里先生的死因审讯中作证——发言人表示，上海公共租界工部局警务处也进行了调查，他推测日方证据和警方证据都将提交。他认为，证人要在英国法庭作证不会有任何异议。

**对温塞特（Wimsett）巡长实施手术**

据昨晚深夜查询，温塞特巡长的状况大致相同，晚间已对他实施了手术。据悉，利里夫人仍遭受严重的神经紧张和休克困扰。

他补充说，在广慈医院（General Hospital），利里夫人称她曾告诉丈夫停车，此言是在她入院后不久作出的。当被追问作出该陈述的具体时间及对象时，翻译回答说：“发言人并非庭审证人，拒绝回答以如此语气提出的问题。”

**警方查询**

当被问及警方是否被允许自由接触两辆肇事车辆的残骸（因为它们不在虹口警察局）时，发言人表示，当光信（Mitsonobu，音译）指挥官于午夜抵达现场时，工部局警务处的调查已经结束。当被问及他是否知晓日本当局或警方已在汽车方向盘上提取指纹的事实时，他回答说对此并不知情。

针对一位询问者提出的“是否有人建议利里夫人及其丈夫前往日本海军陆战队兵营”的问题，发言人表示不存在这种情况，因为他们并未与哨兵交谈。

发言人声称并无此类规定，以此回答了一名记者关于路障是否按照交通法规使用红灯照明的询问。他补充说：“有充足的光线显示这些路障。”

**医院事件**

提及随后在广慈医院发生的事件，据目击者称，一名日本海军军官抵达该院，随行两名水兵刺刀上膛，并在接待大厅来回踱步，用日语发号施令，坚持要查看病人房间及负责医生。一名通讯员问道，是否收到有关日本海军陆战队员访问医院并引发某种“骚乱”的信息。
