“日本军官要求看望伤者，”发言人回答道，“而上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的一名成员擅自拒绝了这一请求，并采取了极不友好的态度。鉴于此，此类事件便会发生，”他补充道。

“我可以反驳这一点，”另一名记者说道，“我当时恰好在那里。这个问题并非由警方提出。”他继续说道，该军官走进事故病房，试图讯问当时已处于四分之三昏迷状态的温塞特巡长。军官接触的唯一一人是那里的电话接线员，后者声明自己只是电话接线员而非医生。此人接着向警方求助。“双方未发一言，日本军官用手指比划出他想看望的病人数目，”他总结道。

**挥拳殴打**

作为回应，发言人表示他并不知晓此事，并质问为何像提问者这样的人能在日本海军军官不被允许进入的情况下获准进入医院急诊室。此时，该记者声明他并未身处急诊室，而是在接待大厅。

“任何人显然都能看出，一辆拖拽着路障的汽车会对方向盘造成阻力，司机应当知道自己拖拽了东西。如果他起初没有这样做，这起不幸的事故就不会发生，”发言人说道，并补充说这并不能为据报道的日本军官的行为开脱。

提及在医院发生的事件，目击者看到一名日本军官用拳头击打上海公共租界工部局警务处助理总监 A. H. 萨姆森（A. H. Samson）先生左耳下方。一名询问者问道，是否会对此名军官采取任何行动。发言人回答说，他目前无法就此发表任何声明。调查仍在进行中，他尚未获悉这些细微细节。

当被问及该公共汽车是否由上海公共租界工部局颁发执照时，发言人表示他不知道。当被问及他是否会进一步查询，因为似乎有一名工部局警务处高级官员遭到日本海军军官殴打，而这似乎并非细枝末节时，发言人表示该案可能会有进一步进展，他目前无法详述细节。

昨日尚不清楚事故原因，因为在确切确定之前，必须对温塞特先生和利里夫人进行问询。据悉，事故发生时路面非常湿滑。经工部局警务处查明，两辆车在相撞时正相向行驶。

CHINA PRESS.
APR 26 1939
Nippon Sentry
Succumbs To
Crash Injury
Correspondent Refutes
Japanese Version Of
Hospital Incident
Rushed to hospital with a crushed skull, the Japanese sentry who rode the running board of Dr. Bertram Lillie's car on Monday night when the vehicle entered a death skid resulting in the tragic end of one of China's most famous education-alists, died yesterday morning in the Japanese military hospital. Caught between the two vehicles, the Japanese bluejacket died before he was able to make a statement to his superiors.
Completely refuting Japanese re-ports regarding the incident which took place in the General Hospital on Monday night, when Assistant Police Commissioner A. H. Samson was alleged to have been struck on the head by a Japanese Naval Landing Party officer, a newspaper reporter gave a vivid eye-witness description of the occurrence before correspondents at the Japanese press conference last night.
A strained atmosphere prevailed at the conference after the subject of the incident had been raised by another correspondent, who asked whether the Japanese Naval spokes-man wished to make any comment on reports which had appeared in all the local newspapers, in connec-tion with the death of Dr. Lillie, principal of the Lester School and Lester Institute of Technical Educa-tion in an automobile crash.
"The Japanese officer asked to see the injured parties, according to the information in the hands of the spokesman," said the interpreter at the conference, "and a member of the Shanghai Municipal Police re-fused to give him permission and adopted an unfriendly attitude— that is why such incidents occur."
Pushed Doctor Aside
"May I contradict that?"—asked a reporter. "I was at the General Hospital when the incident occurred. The officer in question pushed the doctor aside from the entrance to the emergency ward, walked in, and attempted to question Police Ser-geant Wimsett, who was only semi-conscious at that time.
"The police officer was struck without any words being exchanged. The only person who said anything was the hospital telephone opera-tor, who appealed to the police offi-cial 'I am not a doctor. Will you please help me,' when the Japanese officer was trying to question him.
"The police officer walked up to the Japanese officer, and by raising his fingers, indicated that four peo-ple were injured in the accident. The Japanese officer then struck the police official."
"Not An Excuse"
At the conclusion of the state-ment made by the reporter, the naval spokesman stated that "it was impossible for the driver of the car not to have felt the drag of a barricade attached to the rear of the vehicle."

日本哨兵
因车祸伤势
不治身亡

日方关于
医院事件的版本

周一晚间，当伯特伦·利里（Bertram Lillie）博士的汽车陷入致命打滑，导致中国最著名的教育家之一悲剧性丧生时，一名日本哨兵搭乘该车踏板，因颅骨压碎被紧急送往医院，昨晨在日本军医院去世。这名日本水兵被夹在两车之间，在能够向上级作出陈述前便已死亡。

一名报纸记者在昨晚的日本记者招待会上，向日方同行提供了生动的目击描述，彻底驳斥了关于周一晚间在广慈医院发生的事件的日方报道，当时据称警察副总监 A. H. 萨姆森头部遭到日本海军陆战队军官殴打。

在另一位记者提出该事件主题后，会议气氛变得紧张，该记者询问日本海军发言人是否希望就当地所有报纸刊登的、与莱斯特学校（Lester School）及莱斯特技术教育学院院长利里博士死于车祸有关的报道发表评论。

“根据发言人掌握的信息，日本军官要求看望伤者，”会议上的翻译说道，“而上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名成员拒绝给予许可，并采取了不友好的态度——这就是此类事件发生的原因。”

推开医生

“我可以反驳吗？”一名记者问道。“事件发生时我在广慈医院。涉事军官将医生从急诊室入口处推开，走了进去，并试图讯问当时仅半昏迷的警务巡长温塞特。

“该警务官员在未交换只言片语的情况下遭到殴打。唯一说话的人是医院电话接线员，当日本军官试图讯问他时，他向警务官员呼吁‘我不是医生。请帮帮我’。

“该警务官员走向日本军官，举起手指，示意事故中有四人受伤。随后日本殴打了该警务官员。”

“并非借口”

在该记者陈述结束后，海军发言人表示，“汽车司机不可能感觉不到连接在车尾的路障的拖拽力。”

"Is that an excuse for the be-
havior of the officer in the General
Hospital?"—asked a correspondent.
"No. That is not an excuse," re-
plied the spokesman.
"Will any steps be taken to inves-
tigate the officer's behavior?"—it
was asked.
"Minor Points"
"The spokesman has been too pre-
occupied with other matters to at-
tend to minor points such as that,"
the interpreter replied.
"A high official of the Shanghai
Municipal Police is alleged to have
been attacked by a Japanese officer,
and two foreign doctors have been
interfered with while attending to
their patients. Would the naval
spokesman make enquiries into
these reports, which can hardly be
considered 'minor points'?"—asked
a reporter.
The spokesman said that such an
investigation would be made.
Japanese Version
At the outset, the Japanese Navy
spokesman said that he was called
to the scene of the accident late
last night. The accident, he said,
occurred at about 9.20 p.m., when
a motor car proceeding from the
east towards the west crossed
Broadway Bridge over the Hongkew
Creek and hit a barbed wire bar-
ricade.
The car, which was driven by a
Briton, continued to proceed west-
wards, declared the spokesman, al-
though a sentry ordered it to stop.
The car continued for about 100
meters, and was then stopped by a
constable of the Shanghai Munici-
pal Police, near the intersection of
Boone Road and Broadway, still
dragging the barbed-wire barricade
which it had struck.
The constable, continued the
spokesman, boarded the car, which
then returned to Broadway Bridge,
proceeded past the remaining barri-
cade on the bridge, and turned
around.
On Running Board
The Japanese sentry, through a
Japanese civilian who could speak
English, asked the driver why he
had not stopped the car when
called on, the spokesman said, add-
ing that at the time there was
already a member of the Shanghai
Municipal police in the car.
Paying no heed to the sentry, the
spokesman alleged, the driver again
started off over the bridge, but the
Japanese sentry on the other side
of the road jumped on to the run-
ning board and called on the driver
to stop.
It was further alleged by the
spokesman that the driver then
drove his car zig-zag along the road
in an apparent effort to dislodge
the sentry from the running board,
and ran into a bus being driven
along Broadway. "The rest," the
spokesman said, "you know. Dr.
Lillie was killed, his wife and Ser-
geant Wimsett were injured, and
the Japanese sentry died this
morning from his injuries."
Skull Crushed
In reply to a question, the spokes-
man said that the sentry was caught
between the two vehicles when they
crashed. He was never in a state
to make a statement before he died,
as his skull had been crushed.
Asked what witnesses had made
statements to the Japanese authori-
ties in charge of the inquiries, the
spokesman said that the information
released by him was the result of
these inquiries.
In reply to another query on, the
spokesman could see no objection to
any of the witnesses being called by
the British Coroner's Court to give
evidence.

“这能成为该军官在广慈医院行为的借口吗？”一名记者问道。

“不。那不是借口，”发言人回答道。

“是否会采取措施调查该军官的行为？”有人问道。

**“细枝末节”**

“发言人忙于其他事务，无暇顾及此类细枝末节，”翻译回答道。

“据称上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名高级官员遭到日本军官袭击，两名外籍医生在诊治病人时受到干扰。海军发言人是否会调查这些报告？这些报告很难被视为‘细枝末节’吧？”一名记者问道。

发言人表示将进行此类调查。

**日方版本**

起初，日本海军发言人称他于昨晚深夜被召至事故现场。他说，事故发生在晚上9点20分左右，当时一辆由东向西行驶的汽车驶过跨越虹口港的百老汇桥（Broadway Bridge），撞上了一道铁丝网路障。

发言人宣称，尽管哨兵命令其停车，但这辆由一名英国人驾驶的汽车继续向西行驶。汽车继续行驶了约100米，随后在布恩路与百老汇路交汇处附近被上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名巡捕拦停，当时该车仍拖拽着其撞上的铁丝网路障。

发言人继续说，该巡捕登上汽车，该车随后返回百老汇桥，驶过桥上剩余的路障，并掉头。

**站在踏板上**

发言人说，日本哨兵通过一名会说英语的日本平民，询问司机为何在被喝令时未停车，并补充说当时车内已有一名上海公共租界工部局警务处成员。

发言人指控称，司机无视哨兵，再次驾车过桥，但道路另一侧的日本哨兵跳上踏板，喝令司机停车。

发言人进一步指控称，司机随后驾车在路上呈之字形行驶，明显试图将哨兵从踏板上甩下，并撞上了一辆沿百老汇路行驶的公共汽车。“其余部分，”发言人说，“你们都知道。利里博士身亡，其妻子和温塞特巡长受伤，日本哨兵今晨因伤去世。”

**颅骨压碎**

在回答提问时，发言人表示，哨兵在两车相撞时被夹在中间。由于颅骨压碎，他在死前从未处于能够作出陈述的状态。

当被问及有哪些证人向负责调查的日本当局作了陈述时，发言人表示，他所发布的信息正是这些调查的结果。

在回答另一个问题时，发言人表示，他不反对任何证人被英国验尸官法庭传唤作证。

利利夫人的陈述

当被追问利利夫人是否已向日本当局提供陈述时，发言人回答说，她在入院后确实提供了陈述。当被问及陈述是在何时作出的，翻译回答道：“发言人并非受审对象，他对提出这些问题的语气感到不满。”再次受到追问时，翻译称该问题已终结。

当被问及上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）是否获准接触事故残骸时，发言人表示，他相信警务处在残骸被移走之前已在现场完成了调查。他不知道警方是否能够从肇事车辆的轮子上提取指纹。

当被问及虹口港桥梁上的路障是否像道路障碍物通常那样装有红色警示灯时，发言人回答说，虹口地区并未实施此类规定。

死因研讯延期

在身份辨认证据提交后，由登记官莫里斯先生（Mr. Morris）昨日在英国验尸官法庭就利利医生一案开启的死因研讯，被无限期休庭。

阿尔伯特·爱德华·索普先生（Mr. Albert Edward Thorpe）在国际殡仪馆的接待厅提供了身份辨认证据。他是莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院已故校长的同事。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 26 1930

Japanese Sentry Dies
As Result Of Motor Car
Accident In Broadway

Japanese Naval Spokesman Gives Account Of Crash
Which Led To Death Of Mr. Bertram Lillie;
Police Version Is Slightly Different

BARRAGE OF QUESTIONS AT CONFERENCE;
PROTEST PENDING FOR ASSAULT

The second death as the result of the motor car—omnibus crash which took place on Broadway on Monday night, when Mr. Bertram Lillie, Principal of the Lester School and Henry Lester Institute was killed, occurred yesterday morning, as the Japanese Marine, who was on the running board of the car at the time, succumbed to his injuries. He had received a fracture of the skull and made no statement before he died.

With Sergeant R. J. Wimsett, of the S.M.P., and Mrs. Lillie being too ill to be questioned, full investigation into the circumstances leading to the fatal crash could not be completed yesterday. But at the Japanese press conference yesterday afternoon, the Naval spokesman outlined what had been gathered from Japanese witnesses, while a somewhat different version was given in S.M.P. quarters last night.

In outlining his findings of the circumstances leading to the fatal accident, the Japanese Naval Spokesman said yesterday that at about 9.20 p.m. a car proceeding East to West crossed the Hongkew Bridge and in so doing hit a barbed wire barricade. The car did not stop and proceeded westward. The Japanese sentry on the bridge ordered the car to stop, by shouting "Stop" in English.

Did Not Pay Heed

The car did not pay any heed, the spokesman continued, and continued about 100 metres down Broadway, until an S.M.P. officer signalled it to stop. The car stopped at the intersection of Boone Road and Broadway, still dragging the barricade. The S.M.P. officer (who happened to be Sergeant Wimsett) boarded the car and returned with it to the bridge. A Briton was driving the car with a lady being beside him.

The car proceeded past the remaining barricade on the bridge and again turned around and stopped. The Japanese sentry and a Japanese civilian, who spoke English, tried to ascertain why the car did not stop previously. At the time the S.M.P. officer was already in the car. The driver, not paying any heed to the questions asked, started towards the west again.

At that moment, another sentry on the other (north) side of the bridge, jumped on the running board of the car, shouting, "Stop." The lady also shouted, "Stop," the spokesman continued. The driver, however, gathered high speed and proceeded in a zigzag manner as if trying to shake the sentry off the car. Near the intersection of Nanzing Road and Broadway the car ran into an omnibus, the spokesman concluded, as a result of which the foreigner was killed outright, the Japanese sentry died from injuries, yesterday morning, and two other foreigners were seriously injured.

From Police Sources

According to information gathered from S.M.P. sources last night, the barricade on Hongkew Bridge was struck by the car, the driver not stopping. But the car proceeded without being intercepted down Broadway and over the Garden Bridge. When on the south side of Garden Bridge, Mr. Lillie stopped the car and made a report to Sergeant Wimsett whom he saw on duty, and it was decided to go back to Hongkew Bridge to report and explain. It is not quite clear what happened after this, but it does seem well established that Mr. Lillie drove to the south side of Garden Bridge before he took on board Sergeant Wimsett.

Questions At Conference

Following the statement by the Naval spokesman at the Japanese press conference last evening, he was asked from what sources his information was obtained, and he replied that it came from Japanese witnesses. He denied the report made on Monday night that Mr. Lillie had proceeded as far as Garden Bridge and was turned back from there.

Upon being asked whether the Japanese witnesses would be permitted to appear at the British Coroner's Court if so desired, the spokesman stated that an investigation into the accident was also being conducted by the S.M.P., and that the evidence would be combined. He pointed out that he was not in a position to state whether or not the Japanese witnesses would be permitted to appear at the Coroner's Court, but did not think there was any objection.

Mrs. Lillie Said 'Stop'

The spokesman pointed out that Mrs. Lillie had admitted at the hospital that she had told her husband to "Stop". The spokesman could not state when she had made that statement.

《字林西报》
1930年4月26日

日本哨兵死于百老汇路车祸

日本海军发言人讲述导致利利先生死亡的车祸经过；
警方版本略有不同

记者会上连珠炮式提问；就袭击事件待提出抗议

周一晚间发生在百老汇路（Broadway）的汽车与公共汽车相撞事故导致的第二例死亡发生于昨晨，当时站在汽车踏板上的日本海军陆战队员因伤重不治身亡。利利先生是莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特学院的校长，在该事故中丧生。这名日本士兵头部骨折，死前未作任何陈述。

由于上海公共租界工部局警务处的 R. J. 温姆塞特警长和利利夫人病情过重无法接受问询，昨日未能完成对导致这起致命车祸情况的全面调查。但在昨日下午的日本记者招待会上，海军发言人概述了从日本证人处收集到的情况，而昨晚警务处方面给出的说法则略有不同。

在概述其对导致致命事故的情况调查结果时，日本海军发言人昨日称，晚上约9点20分，一辆由东向西行驶的汽车驶过虹口桥，在此过程中撞上了一个铁丝网路障。汽车未停车，继续向西行驶。桥上的日本哨兵用英语高喊“站住”，命令汽车停下。

未予理睬

发言人继续说，汽车未予理睬，沿百老汇路继续行驶了约100米，直到一名警务处警官示意其停下。汽车在布恩路（Boone Road）与百老汇路的交叉口停下，仍拖着路障。警务处警官（碰巧是温姆塞特警长）登上汽车，随车返回桥上。驾车者为一名英国人，身旁坐着一位女士。

汽车驶过桥上剩余的路障，再次掉头停下。日本哨兵和一名会说英语的日本平民试图查明汽车此前为何不停车。当时警务处警官已在车内。司机对提出的问题不予理睬，再次向西启动。

就在那时，桥另一侧（北侧）的另一名哨兵跳上汽车踏板，高喊“站住”。发言人继续说，那位女士也高喊“站住”。然而，司机加速，并呈之字形行驶，似乎试图将哨兵甩下车。发言人总结道，在南京路（Nanzing Road）与百老汇路交叉口附近，汽车撞上了一辆公共汽车，结果导致那名外国人当场死亡，日本哨兵因伤势于昨晨死亡，另有两名外国人重伤。

来自警方消息

根据昨晚从警务处渠道收集的信息，汽车撞上了虹口桥上的路障，司机未停车。但汽车未被拦截，继续沿百老汇路行驶并越过外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）。当到达外白渡桥南侧时，利利先生停下车，向正在执勤的温姆塞特警长报告，并决定返回虹口桥进行报告和解释。此后发生的情况尚不完全清楚，但似乎可以确定的是，利利先生在让温姆塞特警长上车之前，曾驾车前往外白渡桥南侧。

记者会上的提问

在日本海军发言人于昨晚的记者招待会上发表声明后，有人询问他的信息来源，他回答说来自日本证人。他否认了周一晚间关于利利先生曾行至外白渡桥并从那里被折返的报道。

当被问及如果愿意，是否允许日本证人在英国验尸官法庭出庭时，发言人表示，警务处也在对事故进行调查，证据将会合并。他指出，他无权说明是否允许日本证人在验尸官法庭出庭，但他认为没有任何反对理由。

利利夫人曾说“停下”

发言人指出，利利夫人在医院承认她曾告诉丈夫“停下”。发言人无法说明她是在何时作出该陈述的。

"Unfriendly Attitude"

In referring to the subsequent
developments at the General Hospi-
tal, the spokesman said that the
Japanese officers asked to see the
injured parties. They were refused
by a member of the S.M.P., on
his own initiative and in an un-
friendly attitude. "This attitude,"
the spokesman stressed, "accounts
for the incidents."
When this statement was con-
tradicted and it was pointed out
that the Japanese officer had not
asked the S. M. P. officer, but push-
ed past him into the X-Ray room
and attempted himself to question
Sergeant Wimsett, who was on the
operating table at the time, semi-
conscious, the spokesman replied
that he was not aware of that.
The spokesman further pointed
out that if Mr. Lillie had not driven
off, nothing of this nature would
have occurred.
"Is this an excuse for the re-
ported behaviour of the Japanese
officer at the hospital?" he was
asked. "It is not," came back the
prompt reply.
When asked whether steps would
be taken against the officer who
had allegedly slapped the S. M. P.
officer and broken into the X-Ray
room, the spokesman replied that
he was not personally in charge
of the investigation and had not
been informed on all points.
Among the last questions asked
was whether the buses, one of
which was involved in the accid-
ent, carry S. M. C. licences. The
spokesman said he did not know.
Before the matter was dropped
the spokesman was asked whether
he would obtain further informa-
tion on the matter of the alleged
assault of the S. M. P. officer.

Inquest Opened

An inquest on Mr. Lillie's body
was opened in the parlour of the
International Funeral Directors,
Kiaochow Road, by Mr. I. T. Morris,
acting Coroner, yesterday afternoon.
Mr. A. E. Thornton, Registrar of
the Henry Lester Institute of Tech-
nical Education, formally identified
the body as being that of Bertram
Lillie. He had known Mr. Lillie for
nearly six years, he said, and last
saw him alive at about 5 o'clock on
Monday afternoon at the Institute
in Seward Road.
The acting Coroner then adjourn-
ed the inquest sine die, neither Mrs.
Lillie nor Sergeant R. J. Wimsett
being in a condition to give evid-
ence.

当提出关于汽车方向盘上指纹的问题时，发言人否认知晓已提取任何指纹，也无法说明受损车辆被送往何处。当向他指出受损车辆并不在警务处保管之下时，他回答说，警务处已在事故现场结束了查询。

发言人否认日本交通法规规定所有路障都必须照明。当被问及利利先生撞上并沿路拖行的路障是否有照明时，他回答说，桥上有充足的灯光。

“不友好态度”

在提及随后在总医院发生的事态发展时，发言人说，日本军官要求看望伤者。他们遭到一名警务处成员的拒绝，该成员是自行主动并以不友好的态度这样做的。发言人强调：“这种态度导致了后续事件。”

当这一说法遭到反驳，并指出日本军官并未询问警务处警官，而是推开他闯入X光室，并试图亲自讯问当时躺在手术台上、半昏迷状态的温姆塞特警长时，发言人回答说，他对此并不知情。

发言人进一步指出，如果利利先生没有驾车离开，就不会发生此类性质的事情。

有人问道：“这是对据报道的日本军官在医院行为的借口吗？”得到的迅速回答是：“不是。”

当被问及是否会对据称掌掴警务处警官并闯入X光室的军官采取措施时，发言人回答说，他个人不负责该项调查，并未获悉所有细节。

在最后提出的问题中，包括涉及事故的一辆公共汽车是否持有工部局（S. M. C.）执照。发言人表示他不知道。

在结束此事之前，有人询问发言人是否会就据称袭击警务处警官一事获取更多信息。

死因研讯开启

昨日下午，代理验尸官 I. T. 莫里斯先生（Mr. I. T. Morris）在胶州路国际殡仪馆接待厅开启了对利利先生遗体的死因研讯。亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院注册主任 A. E. 桑顿先生（Mr. A. E. Thornton）正式辨认遗体为伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie）。他说，他认识利利先生近六年，最后一次见到他活着是在周一下午5点左右，地点位于西华德路（Seward Road）的学院内。

随后，代理验尸官宣布死因研讯无限期休庭，因为利利夫人和 R. J. 温姆塞特警长均不具备作证的身体条件。

待提出的抗议

从上海公共租界工部局警务处获悉，针对日本海军陆战队一名军官在事故后于总医院据称袭击助理总监 A. H. 桑普森（A. H. Sampson）一事，将通过适当渠道向日本当局提出强烈抗议。

据悉双腿骨折且肋骨断裂的温姆塞特警长于昨晨接受了手术。直到昨日下午晚些时候他才恢复意识，警方尚未能对他进行问询。利利夫人虽然病情不是很严重，但也处于无法接受问询的状态。

病情好转

今晨付印前进行的最新查询得知，利利夫人和温姆塞特警长的病情均有所好转。利利夫人仍受休克困扰，但希望现在可以为温姆塞特的腿部进行复位固定；是否已进行此操作尚无法确定。

MR 26 1939

A REGRETTABLE AFFAIR

As the question of how Mr. Bertram Lillie met his death on Monday night in Hongkew must of necessity be the subject of a judicial inquiry it is not intended at this juncture to discuss the various versions of the matter which were current on the night of the accident, and yesterday. There are, quite obviously, points which can only be cleared up when those who were unfortunate to have been injured will be in a condition to give their evidence. It is impossible, however, to overlook what happened that night at the General Hospital, or to ignore the general indignation which has thereby been aroused. After the accident, in which Mr. Lillie was killed, had occurred, the other occupants of the car who were injured, Mrs. Lillie and Police Sergeant J. R. Wimsett were conveyed with all the speed possible to the General Hospital for attention. It appears that a Japanese sentry had also been hurt, he has since died, and it is to be assumed that the Japanese authorities commenced their investigations in an atmosphere dominated by indignation that one of their men had received harm. That and that alone can explain the truculence, and violence which was demonstrated by certain of the Japanese officials who sought to pursue their inquiries of those of the injured who had been taken to the General Hospital. It appears that a number of Japanese went to the Hospital, with a display of military force, including, it is reported, two machine guns on motor cycles to dominate the entrance. A number of officers and men entered the building and demanded to see the patients. That was of course entirely out of the question. Both Mrs. Lillie and Sergeant Wimsett had had to go on the operating table, and neither of them were in a condition to be questioned. The doctors who refused to permit the Japanese to see them were acting in the only way it was possible for them to do. The condition of both of the patients was such that to have subjected them to questioning under such conditions might have had a serious effect upon them, particularly in the case of Mrs. Lillie who, added to the natural shock of such an occurrence, had the further distressing knowledge that her husband had died at her side.

In the case of Sergeant Wimsett he was on the table in the accident ward, only three parts conscious, and under morphia, when a Japanese entered the room and sought to interrogate him. The doctor in charge of the case had naturally to decline to allow this to go on, and eventually had to remove the injured man to the operating room at the top of the hospital where his treatment was continued behind locked doors. There is also the assault on Assistant Commissioner Samson, which appears to have arisen out of the old familiar language difficulty, which that officer endured with commendable restraint and dignity. The general impression conveyed to the fair number of observers of the whole matter was that the Japanese were behaving with an utter disregard to the sufferings of the injured, which, save for the firmness of the doctors, might actually have impeded the assistance which was being given them. It was not until the arrival of Commander Hayashi, of the Naval Landing-Party that a situation which can be described as nothing less than tense, was relieved, and that officer appears to have acted with a consideration, which up to that moment had been entirely missing. 1939年4月26日

一件令人遗憾的事件

鉴于伯特拉姆·利利（Bertram Lillie）先生周一晚间在虹口身亡一事必然成为司法调查的主题，此时不打算讨论事故发生当晚及昨日流传的各种说法。显然，有些问题只有等到不幸受伤者能够作证时才能澄清。然而，我们无法忽视那晚在总医院发生的情况，也无法无视由此激起的普遍愤慨。在导致利利先生死亡的事故发生后，车内其他受伤的乘客——利利夫人和警长 J. R. 温塞特（J. R. Wimsett）——被尽可能快地送往总医院接受救治。据悉，一名日本哨兵也受了伤，他随后死亡，可以推测日本当局是在其人员受到伤害所引发的愤怒氛围中开始调查的。唯有这一点才能解释某些日本官员在对送往总医院的伤者进行问询时所表现出的好斗和暴力行为。据报道，许多日本人带着军事武力展示前往医院，包括两挺架设在摩托车上的机枪以控制入口。多名军官和士兵进入大楼，要求探视病人。这当然是完全不可接受的。利利夫人和温塞特警长都不得不被送上手术台，两人的状况均不适合接受问话。拒绝允许日本人探视他们的医生采取了唯一可行的做法。两名病人的状况如此危急，若在那种情况下对他们进行问话，可能会对他们产生严重影响，尤其是利利夫人，她在遭受此类事件的自然震惊之余，还面临着丈夫在她身旁去世这一更加令人痛苦的现实。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

APR 26 '39

TRAGIC ACCIDENT
A great amount of sincere public
sympathy has been aroused by reason of
the tragic death of Mr. Bertram Lillie,
Principal of the Lester School and Henry
Lester Institute of Technical Education,
which took place on Monday night in
consequence of a collision between the
motor car he w.. driving and an omnibus
on Broadway. The deceased, who had
occupied his appointment for the past six
years, was an extremely well-known and
popular member of the British community
and had earned for himself the high
opinion of all those connected with the
young but important educational institu-
tion of which he was the head. Mr. Lillie
had been in charge of the Institute from
the time when the work of erecting the
suitable buildings was first put in hand
and it was largely upon the advice which
he tendered that the block in East Seward
Road took shape and eventually opened
with pupils in 1934. The breaking out
of hostilities in August 1937 put the
closure upon the Institute for some time,
though work was carried on in premises
in Edinburgh Road, and it was largely
through the zeal and energies of Mr. Lillie
that resumption of classes in Seward Road
were made possible, under special arrange-
ment, at the end of last summer. It was
tragic indeed that almost immediately
upon his return to Shanghai after a quick
trip to England for the purpose of
engaging an Assistant Master he should
have lost his life at the prime age of 37
years. He was proud of what the Institute
stood for and saw its great possibilities
in a city of this size and importance where
technical education has been sadly lacking.
His many friends here deplore his untimely
death and extend to Mrs. Lillie and her
young daughter Ann their heartfelt
condolences.

《上海泰晤士报》。

1939年4月26日

悲剧性事故

莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特工业技术教育学院院长伯特拉姆·利利先生的悲剧性死亡引发了公众大量真诚的同情，该事故发生在周一晚间，起因是他驾驶的汽车在百老汇路与一辆公共汽车相撞。死者担任该职务已有六年，是英国社区中一位极其知名且受欢迎的人物，赢得了所有与他所领导的这一年轻但重要的教育机构有关人士的高度评价。自着手建造合适校舍的工作开始以来，利利先生一直负责该学院的事务，很大程度上正是基于他提供的建议，位于东熙华德路（East Seward Road）的建筑群得以成型，并最终于1934年招收学生开学。1937年8月战事爆发导致学院关闭了一段时间，尽管在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）的房舍内仍开展工作，而正是凭借利利先生的热情和精力，才使得在去年夏末通过特别安排恢复了在熙华德路的授课。确实具有悲剧色彩的是，在他为了聘请一位助理教员而快速往返英国之后，几乎刚一回到上海，便在37岁的盛年丧生。他为学院所代表的意义感到自豪，并看到了在这座规模宏大、地位重要却严重缺乏技术教育的城市中学院的巨大潜力。他在上海的众多朋友对他的英年早逝表示哀悼，并向利利夫人及其年幼的女儿安（Ann）致以衷心的慰问。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
APR 25 1939

Horrible Hongkew Accident
As Bus Runs Into Car

Mr. Bertram Lillie Killed, Mrs. Lillie Injured ;
Sergt. R. J. Wimsett Seriously Hurt

MR. Bertram Lillie, B.Sc. ENG. (Lond.), A.M.I.C.E., A.M.
I.M.E., principal of the Lester School and Henry Lester
Institute of Technical Education was killed, Mrs. Lillie and Sergt.
R. J. Wimsett of the Shanghai Municipal Police, were seriously
injured in a collision between their car and a Japanese bus on
Broadway near Boone Road, shortly after 9 p.m. last night.
An emergency ambulance arrived on the scene a few minutes
later and all the passengers of the car were rushed to the General
Hospital, where Mr. Lillie was certified dead on arrival, whilst
Mr. Wimsett, it was understood, underwent an emergency operation,
suffering from a fractured left leg and flesh gashes, a cut forehead
and nose and serious other injuries in the face. Mrs. Lillie, is
suffering from serious wounds in the face and from nervous shock
but fortunately, her conditions was not understood to give cause
for anxiety.

At the scene of the mishap, desola-
tion ensued as the bus, which had
been coming along Broadway from
the Garden Bridge, hit the green
Ford sedan which Mr. Lillie was
driving, in the exact middle of the
right side of the body, both doors
being smashed and the welded roof
being forced apart. The rear com-
partment of the car was a pool of
blood, both the seat and the floor
telling a sad tale. It was Mr. Wimsett
who had been sitting in the rear and
who must have lost a considerable
amount of blood before he was re-
moved from the vehicle.
A "North-China Daily News" re-
porter who arrived on the scene only
a few minutes later was prevented
from approaching the car by a num-
ber of Japanese sentries with fixed
bayonets who surrounded the two
vehicles, whilst from the scene of the
accident, as far back as Nanking Road
queue of tramcars were lined up,
which were prevented from moving
into the Baikal Road depot for the
night.
The impact was so terrific, that the
windshield of the bus was smashed,
whilst the radiator and the right
fender were also badly damaged.

Police Officer Assaulted

At the General Hospital, the re-
porter saw a curious sight. Amidst
a number of plain-clothes and uni-
formed members of the Settlement
police, a Japanese officer, presumably
a member of the Naval Landing
Party, accompanied by two guards
with rifles in their hands strode up
and down the reception hall, giving
orders in Japanese and insisting to
be shown to the patients' rooms and
to be taken to the doctors in charge.
He finally approached Mr. A. H.
Samson, Assistant Commissioner of
the S. M. P., and asked him a ques-
tion in Japanese. Mr. Samson's
knowledge of the language was in-
sufficient to understand the officer
whereupon the latter struck Mr.
Samson just below the right ear
with his fist and ordered him out of
the building.
Mr. Samson, with great presence
of mind, stepped back a few paces
and when the officer approached him
once more in a threatening manner,
he left for Hogkew Police Station
although before leaving, he said that
he would come back with the Japan-
ese Superintendent attached to the
station who had been summoned by
telephone but who at 10.15 p.m. had
not arrived at the hospital.

《字林西报》，
1939年4月25日

虹口可怕车祸
公共汽车撞入轿车

伯特拉姆·利利先生身亡，利利夫人受伤；
警长 R. J. 温塞特重伤

伯特拉姆·利利先生，伦敦大学工程学学士（B.Sc. ENG. (Lond.)），英国土木工程师学会准会员（A.M.I.C.E.），英国机械工程师学会准会员（A.M.I.M.E.），莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特工业技术教育学院院长，在昨晚9点过后不久，于百老汇路近 Boone Road 处，其乘坐的轿车与一辆日本公共汽车相撞中身亡，利利夫人和上海公共租界工部局警务处警长 R. J. 温塞特受重伤。
几分钟后，一辆急救救护车抵达现场，车上所有乘客被紧急送往总医院，利利先生抵达时被宣告死亡，而据了解，温塞特先生接受了紧急手术，伤势包括左腿骨折、肉体割裂伤、前额和鼻子割伤以及面部其他严重损伤。利利夫人面部受重伤并伴有神经休克，但幸运的是，据信她的情况并不令人担忧。

在事故现场，悲惨景象随之而来，这辆从外白渡桥沿百老汇路驶来的公共汽车，撞击了利利先生驾驶的绿色福特轿车的右侧车身正中，两扇车门均被撞碎，焊接的车顶被撕裂。轿车后座区变成了一滩血泊，座椅和地板诉说着悲惨的故事。坐在后座的温塞特先生在从车辆中被移出之前，肯定失血过多。
一位仅在几分钟后抵达现场的《字林西报》记者被数名端着刺刀的日本哨兵阻止靠近车辆，这些哨兵包围了两辆车，而从事故现场一直延伸到南京路，排起了长长的电车队列，这些电车被阻止驶入贝加尔路（Baikal Road）车场过夜。

撞击力如此巨大，以致公共汽车的挡风玻璃破碎，散热器和右挡泥板也严重受损。

警官遭袭

在总医院，记者看到了奇特的一幕。在众多便衣和制服的租界警察中间，一名日本军官，推测是海军陆战队成员，在两名手持步枪的卫兵陪同下，在大厅里来回踱步，用日语发号施令，坚持要查看病人房间并被引见给主治医生。他最终走近上海公共租界工部局警务处副督察长 A. H. 萨姆森先生，用日语向他提问。萨姆森先生对该语言的了解不足以理解该军官，于是后者用拳头击打萨姆森先生右耳下方，并命令他离开大楼。
萨姆森先生保持极大的镇定，后退了几步，当该军官再次以威胁姿态接近他时，他前往虹口巡捕房，尽管在离开前他表示，他会随同已通过电话召请但截至晚上10点15分尚未抵达医院的驻站日本巡官一同返回。

（批：FILE）

（批：P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.) 2/4）

pages.en:
Attempted Forcible Entry

Later in the evening, it was understood, the same Japanese officer, together with a few others who had arrived meanwhile, attempted to force his way into the patients' rooms once again but was prevented from doing so by Dr. L. McCulloch and J. G. Anderson, who were attending the patients. When they saw their efforts in this connection fail, they attempted to prevent anyone from leaving the hospital, trying to herd all those present in the hall, into a room for purposes of questioning them.

Another slight incident, just after Mr. Samson was attacked, occurred when the same Japanese officer saw a uniformed sub-inspector of police, carrying the shoes and service-cap belonging to Mr. Wimsett and which had been handed to the sub-inspector by the doctor. The officer suddenly spoke English and asked the police officer where he was taking these things and why. When the officer of the law replied that the doctor had handed them to him, the Japanese desisted.

An hour after the accident about 25 Japanese officers and soldiers were busy on the scene, measuring the width of the road and taking notes, whilst Japanese photographers flashed away and a detective from Hongkew station was making his notes.

Causes Not Yet Known

The causes of the accident are not yet known and both Mrs. Lillie and Mr. Wimsett will have to be questioned before these are definitely established. The car in which the party were riding at the time, was, as far as could be ascertained, coming down Broadway whilst the bus which was on the right side of the road, was coming in the opposite direction. Another factor which will have to be taken into consideration when establishing the causes of the accident, will be the slippery state of the road and whether or not any obstacles were in the way of either of the vehicles.

At a last hour last night, Mrs. Lillie was reported to be resting comfortably and it was presumed that she would return to her home in Weihaiwei Road this morning. Mr. Wimsett's condition was also stated at being satisfactory, although he lost a considerable amount of blood and will definitely be detained for some time. Mr. Wimsett is married and is the father of one child.

Victim Arrives Yesterday

Particularly tragic is the fact, that Mr. Lillie arrived from England yesterday aboard the N.D.L. liner Gneisenau after having been away for only two months to engage a professor of mathematics for the Lester School. He is the father of a three-year-old child. The sad news of her husband's death was not communicated to Mrs. Lillie early last night.

Mr. Lillie, one of the outstanding educators in the Far East, first arrived in Shanghai in 1933 after having spent a number of years in India. He was very popular in educational and social circles locally and his loss will be keenly felt in the various circles in which his work was so much appreciated.
pages.zh:
企图强行闯入

据悉，当晚稍后时候，同一名日本军官连同几名随后到达的人，再次试图强行进入病人房间，但被正在照料病人的 L. 麦卡洛克（L. McCulloch）医生和 J. G. 安德森（J. G. Anderson）医生阻止。当他们看到在此方面的努力失败后，他们试图阻止任何人离开医院，试图将大厅内的所有人赶进一个房间以便进行讯问。

另一件轻微的事件发生在萨姆森先生遇袭后不久，当时同一名日本军官看到一名身穿制服的副督察拿着属于温塞特先生的鞋子和执勤帽，这些物品是由医生交给该副督察的。该军官突然改用英语，询问这名警官要把这些东西带到哪里去以及为什么。当这位执法人员回答说这是医生交给他的时，该日本人便停止了行动。

事故发生约一小时后，约有25名日本军官和士兵在现场忙碌，测量道路宽度并做记录，同时日本摄影师不停拍照，一名来自虹口巡捕房的侦探也在做记录。

原因尚不清楚

事故原因尚不清楚，在确定原因之前，必须对利利夫人和温塞特先生进行问话。据查，事发时当事人乘坐的汽车正沿百老汇路行驶，而位于道路右侧的公共汽车则迎面驶来。在确定事故原因时，还需考虑的另一个因素是路面湿滑状况，以及任何车辆前方是否存在障碍物。

昨晚最后时刻的消息称，利利夫人正在舒适地休息，预计她将于今晨返回威海卫路的家中。据悉温塞特先生的情况也令人满意，尽管他失血较多，肯定需要留院观察一段时间。温塞特先生已婚，育有一子。

受害者昨日抵达

特别具有悲剧色彩的事实是，利利先生昨天乘坐北德意志劳埃德公司（N.D.L.）的“格奈森瑙”号（Gneisenau）邮轮从英国抵达，他此前仅离开两个月，目的是为莱斯特学校聘请一名数学教授。他是一个三岁孩子的父亲。昨晚早些时候，并未将丈夫去世的噩耗告知利利夫人。

利利先生是远东杰出的教育家之一，在印度度过数年后，于1933年首次抵达上海。他在当地的教育界和社交圈非常受欢迎，他的离世将在各个高度评价其工作的圈子中引起深切的悲痛。

CHINA PRESS.
APR 25 1939

Lester Institute Head
Killed, Wife Injured
In Collision With Bus

Bertram Lillie Meets Tragic End On Return
From England; Police Sergeant Wimsett
Seriously Hurt In Hongkew Accident

DEATH SKID ENTERED WITH JAPANESE
SENTRY RIDING ON RUNNING BOARD

Barely six hours after he had returned to Shanghai from leave in
England to take up anew his office as Principal of the Lester School
and Henry Lester Institute of Technical Education, Dr. Bertram Lillie
skidded to death shortly after 9 o'clock last night, at the wheel of a
car he was driving along Hongkew's oil-filmed roads.
Mrs. Lillie, his wife, and Sergeant R. J. Wimsett, of the Shanghai
Municipal Police, were in the car as it skidded broadside on to a
Japanese bus, halted too swiftly at the command of a Japanese sentry,
and both of them were seriously injured. Mrs. Lillie sustained cuts
to the face and forehead, while Sergeant Wimsett suffered a broken
left leg and fracture of the ribs.
Although no detailed account of
the tragedy could be ascertained
last night, it was learned by THE
CHINA PRESS that the crash occurred
at about 9.05 p.m., as Dr. Lillie, Mrs.
Lillie and Sergeant Wimsett were
returning along Minghong Road
from a visit to the Lester Institute
building.

Challenged By Sentry
As the car was about to swing into
Broadway to cross Garden Bridge,
it was reported, a Japanese sentry
challenged the car, and when it
did not stop immediately, jumped on
the running board and shouted to
Dr. Lillie to stop.
The well-known educationallist
immediately stepped heavily on the
brakes and his car went into a skid
across the corner of Minghong Road
and Broadway, on a road surface
made more treacherous by the per-
sistent rain which set in earlier in
the evening.
Swerving wildly across the corner,
the car shot into the path of a
Japanese omnibus proceeding north
from the Garden Bridge and in a
flash had crashed into it.

Car Wrecked
Crumpled beyond recognition, the
car was completely wrecked, and the
front of the bus also badly damaged.
An alarm was turned into the Fire
Brigade for an ambulance, but by
the time the vehicle arrived Dr.
Lillie was dying. Mrs. Lillie and
Sergeant, Wimsett, with Dr. Lillie's
body, were taken to the General
Hospital for treatment, and were
still being detained late last night,
when it was learned that the con-
dition of the injured police officer
was serious.
Japanese naval authorities remov-
ed the sentry who had attempted
to stop the car, and who was flung
headlong from its running board
when the vehicles came in collision.
While no complete report of his in-
juries could be obtained, it was
stated that he also was in a serious
condition. Also slightly injured
were the Japanese driver of the bus,
and a Chinese girl bus conductress,
who received a cut above the right
eye, and suffered shock.

《字林西报》。
1939年4月25日

莱斯特学院负责人
在与公共汽车相撞事故中
身亡，妻子受伤

伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie）从英国归来途中遭遇不幸结局；警佐温姆塞特（Wimsett）在虹口事故中受重伤

死亡漂移发生时车上有日本哨兵站在踏板上

在离开英国休假返回上海、重新担任莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院院长职务仅六小时后，伯特伦·利利博士于昨晚九点刚过不久，驾驶汽车行驶在虹口油污路面上时发生侧滑，不幸身亡。
当时车内还有他的妻子利利夫人以及上海公共租界工部局警务处的 R. J. 温姆塞特警佐。汽车侧滑后横向撞上了一辆因日本哨兵命令而急停的日本公共汽车，两人均受重伤。利利夫人面部和额头割伤，而温姆塞特警佐左腿骨折并伴有肋骨断裂。
尽管昨晚无法获悉该悲剧的详细经过，但据《字林西报》了解，事故发生在晚上9点05分左右，当时利利博士、利利夫人和温姆塞特警佐在访问完莱斯特学院大楼后，正沿明宏路（Minghong Road）返回。

遭哨兵拦阻
据报道，当汽车准备转入百老汇路（Broadway）以穿过外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）时，一名日本哨兵对汽车进行拦阻，因车辆未立即停下，该哨兵跳上汽车踏板，并向利利博士大喊停车。
这位知名教育家立即猛踩刹车，导致汽车在明宏路与百老汇路的拐角处发生侧滑，当晚早些时候开始的持续降雨使路面更加湿滑危险。
汽车在拐角处剧烈转向，冲入了一辆从外白渡桥向北行驶的日本公共汽车的路径中，瞬间与其相撞。

汽车损毁
汽车被撞得面目全非，完全报废，公共汽车的前部也严重受损。
消防队接到呼叫派出救护车，但当车辆到达时，利利博士已奄奄一息。利利夫人、温姆塞特警佐以及利利博士的遗体被送往广慈医院（General Hospital）接受治疗，直到深夜仍被留院观察，此时获悉受伤警官的情况危急。
日本海军当局带走了那名试图拦停汽车、并在两车相撞时被从踏板上甩下的哨兵。虽然无法获得其伤势的完整报告，但据悉他情况也很严重。此外，日本公共汽车司机和一名中国女售票员也受轻伤，后者右眼上方割伤并受到惊吓。

pages.en:
Marines Enter Hospital
Shortly after the accident had occurred, it was stated by authoritative sources last night, a party of Japanese Marines arrived at the General Hospital and demanded to see and interview the victims of the crash.
After refusing to permit the Marines to see Mrs. Lillie and Sergeant Wimsett, it is said, the Hospital authorities eventually permitted them to view Mr. Lillie's body. The Marines are then reported to have threatened to use force unless they were allowed to see Mrs. Lillie's face. At this juncture, a Japanese officer is reported to have arrived on the scene, and after ordering his men back, was permitted to see Mrs. Lillie.
Dr. Lillie, who was born in Durham in 1901, and was educated in the Sunderland Technical College, came to Shanghai in 1933 to open the Lester School and Henry Lester Institute of Technical Education, situated at 505 East Seward Road.

Returned From Leave
Dr. Lillie returned yesterday afternoon to Shanghai by the German steamer Gneisenau after a ten weeks' business visit to England, and was expected to resume his duties with the Institute immediately.
Sergeant Wimsett, whose wife and one child are in Shanghai, was to have left next month on his first long leave. A Yorkshireman, he was an ardent lawn bowls player, and one of the leading darts players in the Force.
It had not been ascertained last night how Sergeant Wimsett came to be in the Lillie's car, but it was assumed that he was returning to the Settlement south of the Creek and asked Dr. Lillie for a lift..

Japanese Report
The Domei new agency reports that Dr. Lillie was "trying to escape" from the sentry when the collision occurred. The injured sentry, according to same source, was First Class Seaman Yoshimori Igarashi, while the driver of the Japanese bus was stated to be Chinese, and not Japanese.
Domei states that the car brushed against a barricade at a Japanese naval sentry post on Broadway Bridge.
Japanese naval authorities started an immediate investigation, but declined to issue an official statement last night.
Traffic was held up on Broadway for some time after the collision. Tramcars proceeding to barns for the night were not permitted to cross Garden Bridge and were lined along the Bund from the bridge to Nanking Road after the accident.
pages.zh:
海军陆战队进入医院
据权威消息人士昨晚称，事故发生后不久，一队日本海军陆战队士兵抵达广慈医院，要求会见并讯问车祸受害者。
据说，医院当局起初拒绝让海军陆战队士兵见利利夫人和温姆塞特警佐，但最终允许他们查看利利先生的遗体。随后据报道，海军陆战队士兵威胁称，除非允许他们看利利夫人的脸，否则将使用武力。在此关头，据报道一名日本军官赶到现场，在命令手下退后后，获准探视利利夫人。
利利博士1901年出生于达勒姆（Durham），曾在桑德兰技术学院（Sunderland Technical College）接受教育，于1933年来到上海，创办了位于西华德路505号（East Seward Road）的莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院。

休假归来
利利博士在赴英国进行为期十周的公务访问后，于昨天下午乘坐德国轮船“格奈森瑙”号（Gneisenau）返回上海，预计将立即恢复在学院的工作。
温姆塞特警佐的妻子和一个孩子在上海，他原定于下个月开始首次长期休假。作为一名约克郡人，他是一名热衷的草地滚球运动员，也是警队中顶尖的飞镖选手之一。
昨晚尚未查明温姆塞特警佐为何会在利利家的车里，但推测他是返回苏州河以南的租界区，并请利利博士顺路载他一程。

日本方面的报道
同盟通讯社（Domei news agency）报道称，碰撞发生时利利博士正“试图逃避”哨兵。据同一消息来源称，受伤的哨兵是一等水兵五十岚吉盛（Yoshimori Igarashi，音译），而日本公共汽车的司机据称为中国人，而非日本人。
同盟社称，汽车在百老汇路桥的日本海军哨所处擦碰了路障。
日本海军当局立即展开调查，但昨晚拒绝发表官方声明。
碰撞发生后，百老汇路的交通受阻一段时间。前往车场过夜的电车不允许通过外白渡桥，事故后被排列在外滩，从大桥一直排到南京路。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 25 1939

Bertram Lillie, Head Of
Lester School, Killed In
Broadway Motor Accident

MRS. LILLIE AND R. J. WIMSETT OF S.M.P.
INJURED WHEN CAR COLLIDES WITH
JAPANESE OPERATED OMNIBUS

JAPANESE MARINE, WHO RODE ON CAR'S
RUNNING BOARD, SERIOUSLY HURT

Twenty Marines Turn-up At General Hospital As
Officers Demand To See Foreign Victims;
Situation Settled By Commander

Only a few hours after he had returned to Shanghai from
a special trip abroad Mr. Bertram Lillie, B.SC.ENG. (Lond.),
A.M.I.C.E., A.M.I.M.E., Principal of the Lester School and Henry
Lester Institute of Technical Education, was killed in an
accident while driving his car on Broadway a few minutes after
nine o'clock last night.

Mrs. Lillie, who was riding with her husband, was badly
injured, as was Mr. R. J. Wimsett, Sergeant of the Shanghai
Municipal Police, who was also in the motor car at the time of
the accident. A Japanese marine, who was allegedly standing
on the running-board of Mr. Lillie's car, when the latter collided
with one of the Japanese operated omnibuses, between Ming-
hong and Boone Roads, was reported to be in a very critical
condition late last night and little hope was held for his recovery.
It was alleged in Japanese quarters that the driver of the car
was attempting to escape.

Despite the fact that the omnibus
was filled with passengers at the
time of the accident, the larger
vehicle withstood the shock much
better than the car, resulting in
slight injuries. The driver of the
bus sustained slight injuries when
the windshield glass was shatter-
ed in front of him; the Chinese con-
ductor also sustained some hurt.

The collision last night was one
of the worst recorded in Shanghai
for a long time. Mr. Lillie's V8-
Ford, licence 5593, was bent beyond
recognition. The right side of the
car, which bore the brunt of the
collision with the omnibus, was
pushed in in one place to the extent
of about 15 inches. The shock broke
the steering wheel, shattered the
window glass and pushed the frame-
work of the car through the roof.

Picked Up Dead

Mr. Lillie is believed to have died
immediately after the crash. He
was pronounced dead upon being
admitted to the hospital, while Mrs.
Lillie and Sergeant Wimsett were
given first aid immediately. Mrs.
Lillia was injured less seriously
than the others, sustaining a frac-
ture of one leg, while Sergeant
Wimsett, it is understood, is suf-
fering from fractured legs, a frac-
tured rib and cut face. The injuries
of the Japanese marine are not
known, but are stated to be very
serious. Standing as he was on
the right running board of the car,
he must have taken the brunt of
the impact.

Up to an early hour this morn-
ing it was not definitely established
how the accident had occurred. No
eye-witnesses could be found, while
the Japanese driver of the bus had
not been questioned by the Shang-
hai Municipal Police. No oppor-
tunity has as yet been found to ques-
tion either Mrs. Lillie or Sergeant
Wimsett.

《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年4月25日

莱斯特学校校长
伯特伦·利利在
百老汇路车祸中身亡

利利夫人及上海公共租界工部局警务处
R. J. 温姆塞特在汽车与
日本运营的公共汽车相撞时受伤

站在汽车踏板上的
日本海军陆战队员受重伤

二十名海军陆战队员出现在广慈医院，
军官要求探视外籍受害者；
事态由指挥官平息

伯特伦·利利先生，理学学士（工程）（伦敦），英国土木工程师学会副会员，英国机械工程师学会副会员，莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院院长，在结束一次特殊的海外行程返回上海仅几小时后，于昨晚九点刚过几分钟，在百老汇路驾驶汽车时遭遇事故身亡。

与丈夫同车的利利夫人严重受伤，当时也在车内的上海公共租界工部局警务处警佐 R. J. 温姆塞特先生同样受伤。一名日本海军陆战队员据称在利利先生的汽车与一辆日本运营的公共汽车在明宏路（Ming-hong）与布恩路（Boone Roads）之间相撞时站在汽车踏板上，据报道昨晚深夜其情况非常危急，康复希望渺茫。日方声称汽车司机当时试图逃逸。

尽管事故发生时公共汽车内坐满了乘客，但这辆较大的车辆比汽车更好地承受了冲击，导致轻微受伤。公交车司机在前挡风玻璃破碎时受轻伤；中国售票员也受了一些伤。

昨晚的碰撞是上海长期以来记录中最严重的事故之一。利利先生的V8福特汽车，牌照5593，被撞得面目全非。承受与公共汽车碰撞主要冲击力的汽车右侧，有一处向内凹陷约15英寸。冲击力折断了方向盘，震碎了车窗玻璃，并将车架顶穿车顶。

确认死亡

据信利利先生在碰撞后立即死亡。他在被送入医院时被宣布死亡，而利利夫人和温姆塞特警佐立即接受了急救。利利夫人的伤势较其他人轻，一条腿骨折，而据了解，温姆塞特警佐双腿骨折、肋骨断裂且面部割伤。日本海军陆战队员的伤势不详，但据称非常严重。由于他站在汽车右侧踏板上，必然承受了冲击的主要力量。

直到今天凌晨早些时候，事故如何发生尚未确切确定。找不到目击者，而公共汽车的日本司机尚未受到上海公共租界工部局警务处的讯问。目前也没有机会讯问利利夫人或温姆塞特警佐。

Immediately after Mrs. Lillie was
taken off the operating table after
splints had been put on her leg, she
asked to be taken home to her little
son, who is down with whooping
cough. This was, of course, out of
the question and Dr. H. Couper Pat-
rick, who attended had her placed
in a ward.

Trouble Arises

Another incident was narrowly
avoided at the General Hospital last
night, when about an hour after the
accident, several officers of the Jap-
anese Naval Landing Party, accom-
panied by about 20 fully armed
marines, arrived and demanded to
see the foreign victims of the ac-
cident.

While the officers went inside the
hospital, accompanied by a couple
of marines with fixed bayonets, the
remainder stood in double file out-
side the entrance to the hospital
and other marines were placed near
the approaches to the hospital. Heat-
ed discussion—participated in by
both foreign and Japanese officers
of the Shanghai Municipal Police,
the Japanese naval officers and Dr.
Patrick—arose when a demand was
made to see the victims.

Dr. Patrick declined to allow this
demand, stating that the patients
were in a serious condition and
could not be disturbed. The Jap-
anese officers insisted and finally
were allowed to see Mr. Lillie's
body. They still persisted in seeing
the other two injured foreigners,
but did not get any satisfaction.
Finally they asked to know in which
rooms they were placed, contem-
plating to place guards outside and
went on to ask to be informed be-
fore either Mrs. Lillie or Sergeant
Wimsett be allowed to leave the hos-
pital.

The whole matter was still un-
decided, with about ten officers and
marines standing about on the
ground floor of the hospital, when
Commander Hayashi of the Japan-
ese Naval Landing Party arrived
at the hospital. The matter was ex-
plained to him and he personally
asked Dr. Patrick to be allowed to
see Mrs. Lillie. He was led to the
room, where she was lying and up-
on returning 10 minutes later, order-
ed all the Naval Landing Party
officers and men to leave the hos-
pital.

He then informed the police offi-
cers present and Dr. Patrick that
the matter was closed. He him-
self remained with Dr. Patrick for
a few more minutes.

Arrived On Gneisenau

Mr. Lillie had just returned yes-
terday afternoon aboard the Nord-
deutscher Lloyd Bremen liner
Gneisenau from a special mission,
which kept him away for ten weeks
from Shanghai. It is understood
that he was driving from the Lester
Institute, with his wife, when the
fatal collision occurred. It was not
known last night how Sergeant
Wimsett happened to be with the
Lillies. Sergeant Wimsett is attach-
ed to the Central Police Station.

Investigation into the accident
was commenced on the spot im-
mediately by officers of the Shang-
hai Municipal Police, the Japanese
Consular Police, the Japanese
Naval Landing Party and the Jap-
anese Military Police. Measure-
ments were taken on the road as
well as photographs of the scene
of the collision.

Domei's Report

According to the version of the
accident obtained by Domei, a motor
car driven by Dr. Lillie, with his
wife and Sgt. Wimsett riding as pas-
sengers, brushed against a barricade
at a Japanese naval sentry post on
Broadway Bridge about 9.20 o'clock
last night while travelling west. Dr.
Lillie had picked up Sgt. Wimsett to
give him a "lift" to the Garden
Bridge.

利利夫人在腿部打上夹板后被抬下手术台，她随即要求回家看望患百日咳的小儿子。这当然是不可能的，主治医生 H. Couper Patrick 博士将她安置在病房中。

发生纠纷

昨晚广慈医院险些发生另一起事件，事故发生约一小时后，几名日本海军陆战队军官 accompanied by 约20名全副武装的海军陆战队员抵达，要求探视事故中的外籍受害者。

当军官们在两名刺刀上膛的海军陆战队员陪同下进入医院时，其余人员在医院入口外双列站立，其他海军陆战队员则部署在医院附近通道处。当提出探视受害者的要求时，引发了激烈争论，参与方包括上海公共租界工部局警务处的外籍和日本警官、日本海军军官以及帕特里克（Patrick）博士。

帕特里克博士拒绝这一要求，称病人情况严重，不得打扰。日本军官坚持己见，最终获准查看利利先生的遗体。他们仍坚持要见另外两名受伤的外国人，但未获满足。最后，他们询问病人所在的房间，意图在门外布置岗哨，并要求在利利夫人或温姆塞特警佐获准离开医院之前通知他们。

整个事项仍未决断，约十名军官和海军陆战队员站在医院一楼大厅时，日本海军陆战队指挥官林（Hayashi，音译）少校抵达医院。向他解释了情况后，他亲自请求帕特里克博士允许他探视利利夫人。他被带到利利夫人躺卧的房间，十分钟后返回，命令所有海军陆战队军官和士兵离开医院。

随后他告知在场的警官和帕特里克博士，此事已了结。他自己又与帕特里克博士停留了几分钟。

乘“格奈森瑙”号抵达

利利先生昨天下午刚刚乘坐北德意志劳埃德不来梅公司的“格奈森瑙”号轮船完成一项特殊使命归来，此次行程使他离开上海十周。据了解，致命碰撞发生时，他正与妻子一起从莱斯特学院驾车离开。昨晚尚不知温姆塞特警佐为何会与利利夫妇同行。温姆塞特警佐隶属于中央巡捕房。

上海公共租界工部局警务处、日本领事警察、日本海军陆战队和日本宪兵队的官员立即在现场开始了对事故的调查。对道路进行了测量，并拍摄了碰撞现场的照片。

同盟社的报道

根据同盟社获得的事故版本，昨晚9点20分左右，利利博士驾驶汽车，载着妻子和温姆塞特警佐作为乘客，向西行驶时，在百老汇路桥的日本海军哨所处擦碰了路障。利利博士搭载温姆塞特警佐是为了让他“搭便车”到外白渡桥。

The "Tairiku Shimpo" publishes
the following leading article under the above headline :-

Gendarmerie and the Japanese Naval Landing Party in the

military zones, despite the existence of the Foreign

Igarashi, first class sailor of the Special Naval Landing

has become celebrated through the arrest of a terrorist
leader who had been disturbing the peace in the vicinity
of Shanghai. The entire Japanese community offers its
deep condolence at the death of Mr. Igarashi.
His death was due to an accident
caused by an Englishman. Mr. Igarashi was posted on sentry
duty, therefore, he has died in action.
The question of the maintenance
of peace and order of Shanghai is a very complicated problem
as the responsible bodies are the Japanese, the British, the
American, the French, the German, the Italian and other
authorities, besides the S.M.P. and the F.M.P. The
FILE residents in Hongkew, whether they are Japanese or foreigners,
are peacefully going about their business in safety under
the protection of the Japanese military authorities.
Effective and suitable measures to suppress anti-Japanese
terrorist groups and anti-Japanese publications which are
disturbing peace and order cannot be adopted because they
are hiding under the shelter of the foreign military and
police authorities. In spite of such obstructions, our
landing party is properly carrying out the important duty

Persons who deliberately pass
our sentry line deserve to be shot dead, but our sentry
restrained from taking direct action in order to respect

attitude of obstruction to Japan in every matter. The

《大陆新报》

“水兵五十岚战死”

《大陆新报》在上述标题下刊登了以下社论：
尽管存在外国租界，上海全体日本侨民高度赞赏日本宪兵队和日本海军陆战队在维护上海及军事区和平与秩序方面所做的工作。特别海军陆战队一等水兵五十岚先生不幸丧生，令人深感遗憾。日本宪兵队因逮捕了一名在上海附近扰乱和平的恐怖分子头目而闻名。全体日本侨民对五十岚先生的逝世表示深切哀悼。
他的死是由一名英国人造成的事故所致。五十岚先生当时正在执行哨兵任务，因此，他是战死沙场。
上海维持和平与秩序的问题是一个非常复杂的问题，因为除了上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）和法租界公董局警务处（F.M.P.）之外，负责机构还包括日本、英国、美国、法国、德国、意大利和其他国家的当局。虹口的居民，无论是日本人还是外国人，在日本军方的保护下，都安全平静地从事着各自的业务。由于反日恐怖团体和反日出版物躲在外国军事和警察当局的庇护下，无法采取有效和适当的措施来镇压这些扰乱和平与秩序的势力。尽管存在此类阻碍，我们的陆战队仍妥善履行着维护上海和平与秩序的重要职责。
故意穿越我方哨兵线的人罪该万死，但我方哨兵为了尽可能尊重第三国国民，克制了采取直接行动。一些英国及其他国籍人员滥用我方哨兵的宽大态度，在穿越我方哨兵线时无视哨兵的喝止，并运送没有通行证的中国人的。
4月24日晚，一名名叫利利（Lillie）的英国人及其妻子两次无视哨兵喝止，穿越我方哨兵线。这是此类事件中最恶劣的一起。该英国人犯罪并导致死亡；此外，当他造成的事故导致我帝国军人之一死亡时，其行为变得不可原谅；他的妻子和一名上海公共租界工部局警务处的警官受伤。
一般而言，英国人误解了日本的动机。日本现在正以巨大的牺牲进行艰苦的斗争，以重建中国和发展新亚洲，然而英国人在每一件事上都采取阻碍日本的态度。

“英国汽车野蛮驾驶：穿越哨兵线：日本海军陆战队员受伤”

“傲慢的英国区巡捕房官员”

车内乘客为莱斯特学校及亨利·莱斯特技术教育学院校长伯特伦·利利（Bertram Lillie）先生、伯特伦·利利夫人以及上海公共租界工部局警务处第310号警员Wimsett先生。伯特伦·利利先生当场死亡，其妻子右眼受伤。该警务处警官左脚骨折并伴有脑出血。三人立即由急救救护车送往北苏州路总医院。

On arrival at the hospital, the
lieutenant requested to be taken to the room where the

租界警卫部队总部的水野（Mizuno）中尉前往医院进行调查。

抵达医院后，中尉要求被带往那位英国女士所在的病房。在上海公共租界工部局警务处C区巡捕房负责人萨姆森（Samson）先生先于中尉抵达医院，他从医院内部出现，并以不尊重的态度拒绝让中尉前往女士的房间，称医院主治医生不允许会见该女士。当被问及女士房间的位置时，他给予了否定的回答。后来他欺骗中尉，先说房间在二楼，后又说在三楼。最终，他将手放在中尉的脸上，中尉对其行为感到非常愤怒，正准备还击但克制住了。

随后，中尉在医院主管帕特里克（Patrick）医生的陪同下进行了面谈，由虹口捕房的须贺（Suga）侦探担任翻译。

医生说：“我并没有拒绝向您展示受伤的英国女士所在的病房。如果陆战队希望如此，我们同意在该女士离开医院时提前通知陆战队。我们也同意陆战队在病房部署警卫。”

因此，医院主治医生向我方陆战队展示了友好态度，这与萨姆森先生所说的相反。
